policy.voice: third-person, present tense, descriptive of the words actually spoken
policy.form: complete sentences; prefer 1 sentence; allow 2-3 sentences when the passage is complex or covers many verses
reviewFlags: structural-change: token Jaccard similarity vs. old text < 0.30 (i.e. >70% structural change)

entries.subcategoryTitle: Nature and Character of the Kingdom
entries.old: Kingdom of heaven compared to a mustard seed — smallest of seeds grows into a large tree sheltering birds
entries.new: Jesus likens the kingdom of heaven to a grain of mustard seed which, though the least of all seeds, grows to become the greatest of herbs and a tree where the birds of the air come and lodge in its branches.

entries.old: The parable of the two sons — one says no but goes, one says yes but does not go
entries.new: Jesus tells of a man with two sons, the first of whom refuses to go work in the vineyard but afterward repents and goes, while the second agrees but does not go, and declares that the publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before those who only profess obedience.

entries.old: The Pharisee and the tax collector — self-righteousness condemned; humility is justified
entries.new: Jesus tells of two men who go up to the temple to pray — a Pharisee who thanks God he is not as other men and recounts his fasts and tithes, and a publican who will not lift up his eyes but smites his breast and asks God to be merciful to him a sinner — and declares that the publican goes down to his house justified rather than the other, for everyone who exalts himself shall be abased and he who humbles himself shall be exalted.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Fig Tree and the Unknown Hour
entries.old: From the fig tree learn its lesson — when the branch is tender, summer is near; when these things happen, the end is near
entries.new: Jesus draws a parable from the fig tree: as its branch becoming tender and putting forth leaves shows that summer is nigh, so when his hearers see all these things they may know that it is near, even at the doors.

entries.old: I AM the Good Shepherd - declaring himself the door of the sheepfold and the good shepherd who knows his sheep, lays down his life for them, and will gather all sheep into one flock under one shepherd
entries.new: Jesus declares that the true shepherd enters the sheepfold by the door and his sheep know his voice, then identifies himself as the door by which any may enter and be saved and as the good shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep, who knows his own as the Father knows him, and who has other sheep not of this fold whom he must also bring, so that there shall be one fold and one shepherd.

entries.old: It is hard for the rich to enter the kingdom — easier for a camel through a needle's eye; with God all things are possible
entries.new: Jesus says that a rich man shall hardly enter the kingdom of heaven — that it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God — and that what is impossible with men is possible with God.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Fig Tree and the Unknown Hour
entries.old: Heaven and earth will pass away, but his words will not; no one knows that day or hour — not the angels, not even the Son
entries.new: Jesus declares that heaven and earth shall pass away but his words shall not pass away, says that of that day and hour knows no man — not the angels of heaven, but the Father only — and likens his coming to a thief whose hour the householder does not know, charging his hearers therefore to be ready.

entries.old: Your Father knows what you need before you ask; he sees what is done in secret and rewards it
entries.new: Jesus teaches that the Father knows what his children need before they ask, and that he sees what is done in secret — in giving, in prayer, and in fasting — and rewards openly.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Promise and Coming of the Spirit
entries.old: He cries on the great day of the feast that if any man thirsts, let him come to him and drink
entries.new: Jesus cries out on the last great day of the feast that if any man thirst, let him come to him and drink.

entries.old: Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand — the time is fulfilled
entries.new: Jesus proclaims that the time is fulfilled and the kingdom of heaven is at hand, calling his hearers to repent and believe the gospel.

entries.old: Entry into the kingdom requires being born again — of water and Spirit; flesh births flesh, Spirit births spirit
entries.new: Jesus tells Nicodemus that except a man be born again he cannot see the kingdom of God, and except he be born of water and of the Spirit he cannot enter the kingdom of God, for that which is born of the flesh is flesh and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: Marvels that the Roman centurion's faith exceeds anything he has found in Israel
entries.new: Jesus marvels at the Roman centurion's faith, saying he has not found so great a faith — no, not in Israel.

entries.old: He has not come to abolish the Law but to fulfill it — not one jot or tittle will pass; whoever relaxes the least commandment will be least in the kingdom
entries.new: Jesus declares that he has not come to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfill them, that till heaven and earth pass not one jot or tittle shall in any wise pass from the law till all be fulfilled, and that whoever breaks the least of these commandments and teaches men so shall be called least in the kingdom of heaven, while whoever does and teaches them shall be called great.

entries.old: Take and eat — this is my body given for you; do this in remembrance of me
entries.new: At the Last Supper Jesus takes bread and the cup, gives them to the disciples, and tells them to take and eat for the bread is his body and to drink for the cup is his blood of the new testament shed for many for the remission of sins, charging them to do this in remembrance of him.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Lord's Prayer — Pattern for Prayer
entries.old: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name
entries.new: Jesus teaches his disciples to pray after this manner, addressing God as their Father in heaven and hallowing his name.

entries.old: He is the true vine, the Father is the vinedresser — every fruitless branch is removed; every fruitful branch is pruned to bear more
entries.new: Jesus declares that he is the true vine and the Father is the husbandman, who takes away every branch in him that bears no fruit and prunes every branch that bears fruit so that it may bring forth more fruit.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Prayer for Himself — The Hour Has Come
entries.old: Father, the hour has come — glorify your Son that he may glorify you; he has authority to give eternal life to all you have given him
entries.new: Jesus prays that the hour is come and asks the Father to glorify the Son so that the Son may glorify him, declaring that the Father has given him power over all flesh to give eternal life to as many as the Father has given him.

entries.old: Names the greatest commandment — love God wholly — with love of neighbor as second, summing up the Law and Prophets
entries.new: Jesus names the first and great commandment as to love the Lord thy God with all thy heart and with all thy soul and with all thy mind, names the second as like unto it — to love thy neighbor as thyself — and declares that on these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.

entries.old: You are the salt of the earth — if it loses its saltiness it is worthless
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples that they are the salt of the earth, and that if the salt has lost its savor it is good for nothing but to be cast out and trodden under foot of men.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Power and Accountability of Words
entries.old: People will give account for every careless word on judgment day — by your words you will be justified or condemned
entries.new: Jesus says that men shall give account for every idle word they speak in the day of judgment, for by their words they shall be justified and by their words they shall be condemned.

entries.old: If earthly fathers give good gifts, how much more will the heavenly Father give good things to those who ask
entries.new: Jesus teaches that if his hearers, being evil, know how to give good gifts to their children, how much more shall their Father in heaven give good things to them that ask him.

entries.old: Not one sparrow falls without the Father's knowledge — even the hairs of your head are numbered; you are worth more
entries.new: Jesus says that not one sparrow falls to the ground without the Father, that the very hairs of his hearers' heads are all numbered, and bids them fear not, for they are of more value than many sparrows.

entries.old: Call no man your father on earth — you have one Father, who is in heaven
entries.new: Jesus charges his hearers to call no man their father upon the earth, for one is their Father, who is in heaven.

entries.old: Tells the Samaritan woman true worship will not be tied to any place — salvation comes from the Jews
entries.new: Jesus tells the Samaritan woman that the hour comes when neither in this mountain nor at Jerusalem shall they worship the Father, and declares that salvation is of the Jews.

entries.old: God is Spirit — those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth; the Father seeks such worshipers
entries.new: Jesus declares that the hour comes and now is when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father seeks such to worship him, and that God is a Spirit and they who worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.

entries.old: Thanks the Father for hiding these things from the wise and revealing them to little children
entries.new: Jesus thanks the Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that he has hid these things from the wise and prudent and revealed them unto babes, for so it seemed good in his sight.

entries.old: With God all things are possible; the Father raises the dead and gives life to whom he will
entries.new: Jesus says that with men it is impossible but with God all things are possible, and that as the Father raises the dead and gives life, so the Son gives life to whom he will.

entries.old: God so loved the world he gave his Son — not to condemn the world but to save it; whoever believes will not perish
entries.new: Jesus declares that God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believes in him should not perish but have everlasting life, for God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world but that the world through him might be saved.

entries.old: No one can come to the Son unless the Father draws him — all the Father gives will come; none can be snatched from his hand
entries.new: Jesus says that all the Father gives him shall come to him and he will in no wise cast out him that comes, and that no man can come to him except the Father who sent him draw him, and he will raise him up at the last day.

entries.old: The Father himself loves those who love Jesus; he has granted the Son authority over all judgment
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples that the Father himself loves them because they have loved him and believed that he came out from God, and that the Father has committed all judgment to the Son.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Lord's Prayer — Pattern for Prayer
entries.old: Your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven
entries.new: Jesus prays for the Father's kingdom to come and his will to be done on earth as it is in heaven.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Lord's Prayer — Pattern for Prayer
entries.old: Give us this day our daily bread
entries.new: Jesus asks the Father to give us this day our daily bread.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Lord's Prayer — Pattern for Prayer
entries.old: Forgive us our debts / sins as we also forgive our debtors
entries.new: Jesus prays that the Father would forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Lord's Prayer — Pattern for Prayer
entries.old: Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil
entries.new: Jesus prays that the Father would lead us not into temptation but deliver us from evil, for his is the kingdom and the power and the glory for ever.

entries.old: Do not pray like hypocrites who stand in public to be seen — go into your room, shut the door, pray in secret
entries.new: Jesus charges his disciples not to pray like the hypocrites who love to stand in the synagogues and on the street corners to be seen of men, but to enter into a closet, shut the door, and pray to the Father in secret, who sees in secret and shall reward openly.

entries.old: Do not heap up empty phrases as the Gentiles do — your Father knows what you need before you ask
entries.new: Jesus warns against the vain repetitions of the heathen who think they shall be heard for their much speaking, for the Father knows what his children need before they ask him.

entries.old: When you stand praying, forgive if you hold anything against anyone
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples that when they stand praying they must forgive anything they hold against any, that the Father in heaven may also forgive their trespasses.

entries.old: Ask and it will be given; seek and you will find; knock and the door will be opened — everyone who asks receives
entries.new: Jesus charges his hearers to ask and it shall be given them, to seek and they shall find, to knock and it shall be opened, for everyone who asks receives, he who seeks finds, and to him who knocks it shall be opened, and asks what father would give his son a stone for bread or a serpent for a fish.

entries.old: This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting — some deliverance requires deeper communion with God
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples that this kind can come forth by nothing but by prayer and fasting.

entries.old: The persistent friend at midnight — a man gives bread not out of friendship but because of shameless persistence
entries.new: Jesus tells of a man who goes to a friend at midnight to ask for three loaves to set before a traveler, and though the friend at first refuses because the door is shut and his children are in bed, yet because of the man's importunity he rises and gives him as many as he needs.

entries.old: The persistent widow and the unjust judge — men ought always to pray and not lose heart; God will give justice to his elect
entries.new: Jesus tells of a widow who keeps coming to an unjust judge that fears not God nor regards man, until at last he avenges her so that she will not weary him with her continual coming, and declares that God shall much more speedily avenge his elect who cry to him day and night, asking whether the Son of man shall find faith on the earth when he comes.

entries.old: Whatever you ask in his name he will do — the Father may be glorified in the Son; ask and you will receive, that your joy may be full
entries.new: Jesus promises that whatsoever his disciples ask in his name he will do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.

entries.old: He chose them to go and bear fruit — that whatever they ask the Father in his name he may give
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples that he has chosen and ordained them to go and bring forth lasting fruit, so that whatsoever they ask the Father in his name he may give it them.

entries.old: Promises a coming day when he will speak plainly about the Father — and they will ask in his name
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples that the time comes when he will no more speak to them in proverbs but show them plainly of the Father, and that in that day they shall ask in his name.

entries.old: Abide in him as the branch in the vine — apart from him you can do nothing; whoever does not abide withers and is burned
entries.new: Jesus charges his disciples to abide in him as the branch abides in the vine, declaring that he is the vine and they are the branches, that whoever abides in him bears much fruit but apart from him can do nothing, and that anyone who does not abide is cast forth as a withered branch and burned.

entries.old: Promises that abiding disciples can ask what they wish — the Father is glorified when they bear much fruit
entries.new: Jesus promises that if his disciples abide in him and his words abide in them they shall ask what they will and it shall be done for them, and declares that the Father is glorified when they bear much fruit and so prove to be his disciples.

entries.old: If you love me, keep my commandments.
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples that if they love him they will keep his commandments.

entries.old: Promises that those who love him and keep his word will be loved by the Father — and the Father and Son will dwell with them
entries.new: Jesus promises that whoever loves him will keep his words and will be loved by the Father, and that he and the Father will come to that one and make their abode with him, while whoever does not love him does not keep his sayings — and the word they hear is not his but the Father's who sent him.

entries.old: They are already clean through the word he has spoken to them.
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples that they are already clean through the word he has spoken to them.

entries.old: As the Father has loved him, so has he loved them — abide in his love by keeping his commandments, as he kept the Father's
entries.new: Jesus declares that as the Father has loved him so he has loved his disciples, and charges them to continue in his love by keeping his commandments, even as he has kept his Father's commandments and abides in his love.

entries.old: These things he has spoken so that his joy may be in them and their joy may be full
entries.new: Jesus says that he has spoken these things to his disciples so that his joy might remain in them and that their joy might be full.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Prayer for Himself — The Hour Has Come
entries.old: Defines eternal life — knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he sent
entries.new: Jesus prays that life eternal is to know the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he has sent.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Prayer for Himself — The Hour Has Come
entries.old: Asks the Father to glorify him with the glory they shared before the world existed
entries.new: Jesus tells the Father he has glorified him on the earth and finished the work given him to do, and asks the Father to glorify him now with the glory which he had with him before the world was.

entries.old: Prays for those the Father has given him — that they be kept united and protected from the evil one
entries.new: Jesus says he has manifested the Father's name to the men given him out of the world, and prays not for the world but for those the Father has given him, asking the Holy Father to keep them through his own name that they may be one as he and the Father are one, and not to take them out of the world but to keep them from the evil.

entries.old: Acknowledges the disciples have received his words and believed the Father sent him
entries.new: Jesus tells the Father that the disciples have known that all things given him are from the Father, having received the words he gave them and known surely that he came forth from him and believed that the Father sent him.

entries.old: All things that are his are the Father's, and all that are the Father's are his — and he is glorified in his disciples.
entries.new: Jesus declares to the Father that all his are the Father's and all the Father's are his, and that he is glorified in them.

entries.old: Tells the Father he kept all but the son of perdition — now he prays the disciples may have his joy though the world hates them
entries.new: Jesus tells the Father that while he was with the disciples in the world he kept them in his name and none was lost but the son of perdition, that the scripture might be fulfilled, and that he speaks these things so they may have his joy fulfilled in themselves, having given them the Father's word though the world has hated them because they are not of the world, even as he is not of the world.

entries.old: Tells the Father his disciples do not belong to the world, just as he does not
entries.new: Jesus says that his disciples are not of the world, even as he is not of the world.

entries.old: Sanctify them in the truth — your word is truth; as the Father sent him into the world, he sends them; for their sake he consecrates himself
entries.new: Jesus prays that the Father sanctify the disciples through his truth, declaring that his word is truth, and that as the Father has sent him into the world he has likewise sent them into the world, and for their sakes he sanctifies himself that they also may be sanctified through the truth.

entries.old: Prays for all future believers — that their unity may mirror the Father and Son and testify the Father sent him
entries.new: Jesus prays not only for the disciples but also for all who shall believe on him through their word, that they all may be one as the Father is in him and he in the Father, that they also may be one in them so the world may believe that the Father has sent him, and that being made perfect in one the world may know the Father loved them as he loved him.

entries.old: Asks that the disciples be with him to see his glory — and that the Father's love would dwell in them
entries.new: Jesus tells the Father he has given the disciples the glory the Father gave him, and wills that those given him be with him where he is to behold his glory which the Father gave him before the foundation of the world, having declared the Father's name to them so that the love with which the Father loved him may be in them, and he in them.

entries.old: O righteous Father, the world has not known you, but he has known you, and these have known that you sent him.
entries.new: Jesus calls upon the righteous Father, saying that the world has not known him, but he has known him, and these have known that the Father sent him.

entries.old: The Good Samaritan — a despised outsider shows mercy to the man left for dead; go and do likewise
entries.new: Jesus tells of a man going down from Jerusalem to Jericho who falls among thieves and is left half dead, whom a priest and a Levite pass by on the other side, but a Samaritan has compassion, binds up his wounds with oil and wine, brings him to an inn, and pays the host to care for him, and asks which of the three was neighbour to the wounded man, charging his hearer to go and do likewise.

entries.old: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, pray for those who persecute you — be merciful as the Father is merciful
entries.new: Jesus says to love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you and persecute you, calling his hearers to be merciful as their Father is merciful.

entries.old: If you love only those who love you, what reward do you have? Even tax collectors do the same; lend expecting nothing in return
entries.new: Jesus asks what reward there is in loving only those who love you or saluting only your brethren, since even the publicans do the same, and charges his hearers to lend hoping for nothing in return.

entries.old: A new commandment: love one another as I have loved you — by this all will know you are his disciples
entries.new: Jesus gives a new commandment, that his disciples love one another as he has loved them, and says by this shall all men know they are his disciples, if they have love one to another.

entries.old: Greater love has no one than this: to lay down his life for his friends; you are his friends if you do what he commands
entries.new: Jesus declares that greater love has no man than to lay down his life for his friends, and tells his disciples they are his friends if they do whatsoever he commands them.

entries.old: He no longer calls them servants but friends — he has made known everything he heard from the Father
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples that he no longer calls them servants, since the servant does not know what his lord does, but calls them friends, for he has made known to them all things he has heard from his Father.

entries.old: You are the light of the world — a city on a hill cannot be hidden; let your light shine so others may glorify the Father
entries.new: Jesus tells his hearers that they are the light of the world, that a city set on a hill cannot be hid and a candle is not lit to be put under a bushel but on a candlestick, and charges them to let their light so shine before men that others may see their good works and glorify their Father in heaven.

entries.old: He has not come to abolish the Law but to fulfill it — not one jot or tittle will pass; whoever relaxes even the least commandment will be least in the kingdom
entries.new: Jesus declares that he has not come to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfill them, that till heaven and earth pass not one jot or tittle shall pass from the law, and that whoever breaks the least of these commandments and teaches men so shall be called least in the kingdom of heaven, while the one who does and teaches them shall be called great.

entries.old: Sets the standard for kingdom entry — righteousness that surpasses the scribes and Pharisees
entries.new: Jesus says that unless his hearers' righteousness exceeds the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, they shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Antitheses — “You Have Heard… But I Say to You”
entries.old: Anger: murder begins in the heart — contempt and insult bring one into judgment
entries.new: Jesus teaches that while it was said of old that whoever kills shall be in danger of judgment, whoever is angry with his brother without cause shall also be in danger of judgment, whoever says Raca shall be in danger of the council, and whoever says Thou fool shall be in danger of hell fire.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Antitheses — “You Have Heard… But I Say to You”
entries.old: Lust: adultery begins with a lustful look; if eye or hand causes sin, remove it
entries.new: Jesus teaches that whoever looks on a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart, and that if the right eye or right hand offends, it is better to pluck it out or cut it off and cast it away than to have the whole body cast into hell.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Antitheses — “You Have Heard… But I Say to You”
entries.old: Divorce: a certificate of divorce causes adultery, except for sexual immorality
entries.new: Jesus says that whoever puts away his wife, except for the cause of fornication, causes her to commit adultery, and whoever marries her that is divorced commits adultery.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Antitheses — “You Have Heard… But I Say to You”
entries.old: Oaths: do not swear at all — let your yes be yes and your no be no; anything more is from evil
entries.new: Jesus charges his hearers to swear not at all — neither by heaven, for it is God's throne, nor by the earth, his footstool, nor by Jerusalem, nor by their own head — but to let their communication be Yea, yea and Nay, nay, for whatever is more than these comes of evil.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Antitheses — “You Have Heard… But I Say to You”
entries.old: Retaliation: do not resist the evil one — turn the other cheek, give your cloak, go the extra mile
entries.new: Jesus teaches his hearers not to resist evil but to turn the other cheek when smitten, to let the one who sues for their coat have their cloak also, to go two miles with whoever compels them to go one, and to give to him that asks and not turn away from him that would borrow.

entries.old: Give in secret, not before others to be seen — your Father who sees in secret will reward you
entries.new: Jesus warns his hearers not to do their alms before men to be seen of them, nor to sound a trumpet as the hypocrites do who already have their reward, but to give so that the left hand knows not what the right hand does, and the Father who sees in secret shall reward them openly.

entries.old: Fast without showing it — anoint your head, wash your face; true piety is seen by God alone
entries.new: Jesus charges his hearers, when they fast, not to be of a sad countenance like the hypocrites who disfigure their faces to appear unto men to fast, but to anoint the head and wash the face so that the fast is seen not by men but by the Father in secret, who shall reward them openly.

entries.old: Do not judge, or you will be judged — first remove the log from your own eye, then help your brother with his
entries.new: Jesus says, Judge not, that ye be not judged, for with the same judgment and measure they use it shall be measured to them again, and asks why they behold the mote in their brother's eye but consider not the beam in their own, charging the hypocrite first to cast the beam from his own eye, that he may then see clearly to remove the mote from his brother's.

entries.old: Do not give what is holy to dogs or pearls to pigs; judge with righteous judgment, not by appearances
entries.new: Jesus charges his hearers not to give that which is holy unto the dogs nor to cast their pearls before swine, lest they be trampled under foot and the swine turn again and rend them.

entries.old: He tells the accusers of the woman caught in adultery that he who is without sin among them should cast the first stone
entries.new: Jesus tells the accusers of the woman caught in adultery that he who is without sin among them should cast the first stone at her.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Golden Rule and Two Ways
entries.old: Whatever you wish others would do to you, do also to them — this is the Law and the Prophets
entries.new: Jesus teaches that whatever his hearers would have men do to them, they should do even so to them, for this is the law and the prophets.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Golden Rule and Two Ways
entries.old: He who hears his words and does them is like a wise man who built on rock; who hears but does not act built on sand
entries.new: Jesus likens whoever hears his sayings and does them to a wise man who built his house upon a rock, which stood when the rain descended and the floods came and the winds blew, and likens whoever hears them but does them not to a foolish man who built his house upon the sand, which fell, and great was its fall.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature of Greatness in the Kingdom
entries.old: Whoever receives a child in his name receives him — the least among all is the greatest
entries.new: Jesus declares that whoever receives one such little child in his name receives him.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature of Greatness in the Kingdom
entries.old: Reverses worldly ranks in the kingdom — but many that are first shall be last, and the last shall be first
entries.new: Jesus says that many that are first shall be last, and the last shall be first.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature of Greatness in the Kingdom
entries.old: Whoever would be great must be a servant — whoever would be first must be slave of all; the last will be first
entries.new: Jesus tells the mother of Zebedee's sons and the disciples that they know not what they ask, that to drink his cup and be baptized with his baptism is theirs but to sit at his right or left is the Father's to give, and charges them that unlike the princes of the Gentiles who exercise dominion, whoever would be great among them must be their minister and whoever would be chief must be their servant.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature of Greatness in the Kingdom
entries.old: Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled; whoever humbles himself will be exalted; the greatest is the servant of all
entries.new: Jesus declares that the greatest among them shall be their servant, and that whoever exalts himself shall be abased while whoever humbles himself shall be exalted.

entries.old: The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve and give his life as a ransom for many
entries.new: Jesus says that the Son of man came not to be ministered unto but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.

entries.old: What he is doing Peter does not now understand but will know later — and unless Peter is washed, he has no part with Jesus.
entries.new: Jesus tells Peter that what he does Peter knows not now but shall know hereafter, and that if he washes him not, Peter has no part with him.

entries.old: Tells Peter the bathed person needs only their feet washed — and the disciples are clean, though not all
entries.new: Jesus says that he who is washed needs only to wash his feet but is clean every whit, and that the disciples are clean, but not all of them.

entries.old: He asks if they understand what he has done; they rightly call him Master and Lord, for so he is.
entries.new: Jesus asks the disciples whether they know what he has done to them, and affirms that they say well in calling him Master and Lord, for so he is.

entries.old: After washing the disciples' feet, calls them to do likewise — the servant is not greater than the master
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples that since he, their Lord and Master, has washed their feet, they also ought to wash one another's feet, for he has given them an example, and declares that the servant is not greater than his lord nor he that is sent greater than he that sent him, and that they are happy if they do these things.

entries.old: Do not take the seat of honor — sit in the lowest place; when you give a banquet, invite those who cannot repay you
entries.new: Jesus tells those bidden to a wedding not to sit down in the highest room lest a more honourable man come and they be put to shame, but to take the lowest room so the host may say, Friend, go up higher; for whoever exalts himself shall be abased and he that humbles himself shall be exalted, and he charges them when they make a feast to call not their friends or rich neighbors but the poor, the maimed, the lame, and the blind, who cannot recompense them, so that they shall be recompensed at the resurrection of the just.

entries.old: Teaches that disciples obeying every command are still unworthy servants — duty earns no praise
entries.new: Jesus tells of a servant who comes from plowing or feeding cattle and is told first to make ready his master's meal and serve him before eating himself, and asks whether the master thanks the servant for doing what was commanded; so likewise, when the disciples have done all they were commanded, they are to say, We are unprofitable servants, we have done that which was our duty to do.

entries.old: Calls disciples to become like little children — only the humble enter the kingdom and are greatest in it
entries.new: Jesus declares that except his hearers be converted and become as little children they shall not enter the kingdom of heaven, and that whoever humbles himself as a little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.

entries.old: Defends the children's praise in the temple by quoting Psalm 8 — God ordains praise from the mouths of infants
entries.new: Jesus answers the chief priests and scribes by asking whether they have never read that out of the mouth of babes and sucklings God has perfected praise.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Power and Accountability of Words
entries.old: What comes out of the mouth proceeds from the heart — this is what defiles a person
entries.new: Jesus teaches that the things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart, and these defile the man.

entries.old: His testimony is valid — he knows where he came from; two witnesses confirm truth: himself and the Father
entries.new: Jesus declares that his record of himself is true because he knows whence he came and whither he goes, and that under the law the testimony of two men is true — he bears witness of himself, and the Father who sent him also bears witness of him.

entries.old: You will know the truth and the truth will set you free; if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed
entries.new: Jesus says that his hearers shall know the truth and the truth shall make them free, and that if the Son makes them free they shall be free indeed.

entries.old: Declares himself the way, the truth, and the life — no one comes to the Father except through him
entries.new: Jesus declares that he is the way, the truth, and the life, and that no man comes to the Father but by him.

entries.old: He who has ears to hear, let him hear — a call to spiritual attention repeated throughout his ministry
entries.new: Jesus repeats his summons that he who has ears to hear, let him hear, calling his hearers throughout his ministry to give spiritual attention to his words.

entries.old: Tells the disciples kingdom mysteries are given to them — others see and hear without perceiving
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples that it is given them to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven but not to others, that he speaks to the multitude in parables because seeing they see not and hearing they hear not, and blesses his disciples' eyes and ears, declaring that many prophets and righteous men desired to see and hear what they now see and hear.

entries.old: Summons the multitude to attend his teaching on defilement — hear, and understand
entries.new: Jesus calls the multitude to him and charges them to hear and understand.

entries.old: Rebukes the disciples' dullness — what enters the mouth simply passes through, but what comes out defiles
entries.new: Jesus asks his disciples whether they are also yet without understanding, that whatever enters in at the mouth goes into the belly and is cast out into the draught.

entries.old: Pay attention to what you hear — to the one who has, more will be given; from the one who has not, even what he has will be taken
entries.new: Jesus charges his hearers to take heed what they hear, for with the measure they mete it shall be measured to them, and to him that has more shall be given, while from him that has not shall be taken even that which he has.

entries.old: If any man have ears to hear, let him hear — Jesus presses the multitude to receive the teaching
entries.new: Jesus declares that if any man have ears to hear, let him hear.

entries.old: The Pharisees are blind guides of the blind — both fall into a pit; you can read the sky but not the signs of the times
entries.new: Jesus says to let the Pharisees alone, for they are blind leaders of the blind, and if the blind lead the blind both shall fall into the ditch.

entries.old: Rebukes the Pharisees and Sadducees — they read the weather but cannot discern the signs of the times
entries.new: Jesus tells the Pharisees and Sadducees that when it is evening they say it will be fair weather, for the sky is red.

entries.old: Refuses the Pharisees' demand for a sign — no sign will be given to this generation
entries.new: Jesus asks why this generation seeks after a sign, and declares that verily there shall no sign be given to this generation.

entries.old: Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod — guard your hearts from their teaching
entries.new: Jesus charges his disciples to take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the leaven of Herod.

entries.old: Rebukes the disciples for missing the bread analogy — they have eyes and ears yet still do not understand
entries.new: Jesus rebukes the disciples for reasoning that they have no bread, asking whether they yet perceive nor understand, whether their hearts are hardened, and whether having eyes they see not and having ears they hear not, then reminds them of the baskets gathered after the five loaves among five thousand and the seven among four thousand, and asks how it is they do not understand.

entries.old: Tells the crowd they predict the weather expertly but cannot discern the present time
entries.new: Jesus tells the people that when they see a cloud rise out of the west they say a shower is coming, and when the south wind blows they say there will be heat, and so it comes to pass.

entries.old: Declares his coming inverts sight — the unseeing receive sight, the self-confident are made blind
entries.new: Jesus declares that for judgment he is come into this world, that they which see not might see and they which see might be made blind.

entries.old: Because you say “I see” — your guilt remains; you search the Scriptures thinking they give life, yet refuse to come to him
entries.new: Jesus tells the Pharisees that if they were blind they should have no sin, but because they say they see, their sin remains.

entries.old: Beware of false prophets in sheep's clothing — you will know them by their fruits; a good tree cannot bear bad fruit
entries.new: Jesus warns his hearers to beware of false prophets who come in sheep's clothing but inwardly are ravening wolves, declaring that they shall be known by their fruits, for men do not gather grapes of thorns or figs of thistles, a good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit nor a corrupt tree good fruit, and every tree that brings not forth good fruit is hewn down and cast into the fire.

entries.old: Teaches the tree is known by its fruit — the mouth speaks from the abundance of the heart
entries.new: Jesus teaches that the tree is known by its fruit, calls his hearers a generation of vipers and asks how, being evil, they can speak good things, for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks, and a good man brings forth good things from the good treasure of his heart while an evil man brings forth evil things from the evil treasure.

entries.old: Warns the disciples to guard against the hypocrisy of the Pharisees
entries.new: Jesus charges his disciples to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

entries.old: Beware of false christs and false prophets who perform great signs to deceive, if possible, even the elect
entries.new: Jesus warns that if any shall say to them, behold, here is Christ or there, they are not to believe it, for false christs and false prophets shall arise and shew great signs and wonders to deceive, if possible, even the elect, and charges them not to go forth whether they are told he is in the desert or in the secret chambers.

entries.old: Names the verdict — light came into the world but people loved darkness because their deeds were evil
entries.new: Jesus declares that this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world and men loved darkness rather than light because their deeds were evil, for everyone that does evil hates the light lest his deeds be reproved, but he that does truth comes to the light that his deeds may be made manifest as wrought in God.

entries.old: Nothing is covered that will not be uncovered — what is whispered in private will be proclaimed on the housetops
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples not to fear, for there is nothing covered that shall not be revealed nor hid that shall not be known, and what he tells them in darkness they are to speak in light, and what they hear in the ear they are to preach upon the housetops.

entries.old: A lamp is not brought in to be hidden — nothing is secret except to come to light
entries.new: Jesus asks whether a candle is brought to be put under a bushel or under a bed and not to be set on a candlestick, declaring that there is nothing hid which shall not be manifested, neither anything kept secret but that it should come abroad.

entries.old: Your sins are forgiven — the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins
entries.new: Jesus declares to the man sick of the palsy that his sins are forgiven, and when the scribes reason in their hearts that this is blasphemy, he asks whether it is easier to say thy sins be forgiven thee or to say arise and walk, then heals the man so they may know that the Son of man has power on earth to forgive sins.

entries.old: Two debtors forgiven by a creditor — the one forgiven most loves most; this woman has loved much, while Simon offered no water, kiss, or oil
entries.new: Jesus tells Simon the Pharisee of a creditor who frankly forgave two debtors, one owing five hundred pence and the other fifty, and asks which will love him most; when Simon answers the one forgiven more, Jesus contrasts the woman who has washed his feet with tears, kissed them, and anointed them with ointment against Simon, who gave him no water, no kiss, and no oil.

entries.old: The one forgiven much loves much — the one forgiven little loves little
entries.new: Jesus declares that the woman's many sins are forgiven because she loved much, and that the one to whom little is forgiven loves little.

entries.old: If you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will forgive you — but if you do not forgive, he will not forgive your trespasses either
entries.new: Jesus teaches that if his hearers forgive men their trespasses, the heavenly Father will also forgive them, but if they do not forgive men, neither will the Father forgive their trespasses.

entries.old: Forgive not seven times but seventy-seven / seventy times seven — without limit
entries.new: Jesus answers Peter that he is not to forgive a brother seven times but until seventy times seven.

entries.old: The unforgiving servant — forgiven a vast debt, he refuses to forgive a small one
entries.new: Jesus likens the kingdom of heaven to a king who, moved with compassion, forgives a servant his debt of ten thousand talents, but when that servant goes out and seizes a fellowservant who owes him a hundred pence, casting him into prison until the debt is paid, the lord delivers the wicked servant to the tormentors and warns that so likewise his heavenly Father shall do to them if they do not from their hearts forgive every brother his trespasses.

entries.old: Warns that those who refuse to forgive will not be forgiven by the Father
entries.new: Jesus warns that if his hearers do not forgive, neither will their Father in heaven forgive their trespasses.

entries.old: Leave your gift at the altar — first be reconciled to your brother, then come and offer it
entries.new: Jesus charges that if one brings a gift to the altar and there remembers that a brother has aught against him, he is to leave the gift before the altar, go and first be reconciled to the brother, and then come and offer the gift.

entries.old: Settle matters quickly with your adversary while on the way
entries.new: Jesus counsels his hearers to agree with their adversary quickly while still in the way with him, lest the adversary deliver them to the judge and the judge to the officer and they be cast into prison, from which they shall by no means come out till they have paid the uttermost farthing.

entries.old: If your brother sins against you, go privately — if he listens, you have won him; take witnesses; then tell the church
entries.new: Jesus instructs that if a brother trespasses, one is to go and tell him his fault between the two of them alone, and if he hears, the brother is gained; if he will not hear, to take one or two more so that every word is established by witnesses; if he still will not hear, to tell it to the church; and if he refuses to hear the church, to let him be as a heathen man and a publican.

entries.old: Whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery
entries.new: Jesus declares that whoever puts away his wife, except for the cause of fornication, causes her to commit adultery, and that whoever marries her who is divorced commits adultery.

entries.old: From the beginning God made them male and female — what God has joined, let no one separate; Moses permitted divorce only because of hardness of heart
entries.new: Jesus says that he who made them at the beginning made them male and female, that for this cause a man shall leave father and mother and cleave to his wife and the two shall be one flesh, that what God has joined together let not man put asunder, and that Moses suffered them to put away their wives only because of the hardness of their hearts, but from the beginning it was not so.

entries.old: Teaches that some forgo marriage for the kingdom — those able to accept this calling should do so
entries.new: Jesus says that not all men can receive this saying but only those to whom it is given, naming eunuchs born so from the womb, eunuchs made by men, and those who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven's sake, and bids him that is able to receive it to receive it.

entries.old: In the resurrection, people neither marry nor are given in marriage — they are like angels
entries.new: Jesus tells the Sadducees that they err, not knowing the scriptures nor the power of God, that in the resurrection people neither marry nor are given in marriage but are as the angels of God in heaven, and that God is not the God of the dead but of the living, being the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

entries.old: What comes out of a person defiles him — from within come sexual immorality, adultery, and licentiousness
entries.new: Jesus teaches that out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, and blasphemies.

entries.old: He came not to bring peace but division — households will be divided; whoever does the will of God is his true family
entries.new: Jesus says he came not to send peace on earth but a sword, to set a man at variance against his father, the daughter against her mother, and the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law, and that a man's foes shall be those of his own household.

entries.old: Honor your father and mother; yet whoever loves family more than Jesus is not worthy of him
entries.new: Jesus declares that he who loves father or mother more than him is not worthy of him, and he who loves son or daughter more than him is not worthy of him.

entries.old: Who is my mother, or my brethren? Behold my mother and my brethren — those who do God's will are my true family
entries.new: Jesus asks who is his mother and his brethren, then looking around on those who sit about him names them as his mother and his brethren.

entries.old: Identifies his true family as those who hear and obey the word of God
entries.new: Jesus names his mother and his brethren as those who hear the word of God and do it.

entries.old: Whoever causes one of these little ones to stumble — better a millstone around his neck; do not despise them
entries.new: Jesus warns that whoever offends one of these little ones who believe in him would be better off with a millstone hanged about his neck and drowned in the depth of the sea, pronounces woe on the world because of offenses and on the man by whom the offense comes, and charges his hearers not to despise one of these little ones, for in heaven their angels always behold the face of his Father.

entries.old: Let the little children come — do not hinder them; to such belongs the kingdom of heaven
entries.new: Jesus bids his disciples suffer the little children to come to him and forbid them not, for of such is the kingdom of heaven.

entries.old: Do not store up earthly treasure — store up in heaven; where your treasure is, your heart will be also
entries.new: Jesus teaches his hearers not to lay up for themselves treasures upon earth where moth and rust corrupt and thieves break through and steal, but to lay up treasures in heaven where neither moth nor rust corrupts nor thieves break through, for where their treasure is there will their heart be also.

entries.old: The eye is the lamp of the body — if your eye is healthy, your whole body is full of light
entries.new: Jesus says that the light of the body is the eye, that if the eye be single the whole body shall be full of light, but if the eye be evil the whole body shall be full of darkness, and asks how great that darkness is if the light within be darkness.

entries.old: No one can serve two masters — you cannot serve both God and money
entries.new: Jesus declares that no man can serve two masters, for he will either hate the one and love the other or hold to the one and despise the other, and that his hearers cannot serve God and mammon.

entries.old: Refuses to arbitrate an inheritance dispute — and warns the crowd against covetousness
entries.new: Jesus refuses to arbitrate an inheritance dispute between two brothers, asking who made him a judge or a divider over them.

entries.old: Woe to the rich and full — they have received their consolation
entries.new: Jesus pronounces woe upon those who are rich, for they have received their consolation, and woe upon those who are full and those who laugh now, for they shall hunger, mourn, and weep.

entries.old: The rich fool — his soul is required the very night he builds bigger barns; life does not consist in abundance of possessions
entries.new: Jesus warns against covetousness, saying a man's life consists not in the abundance of the things he possesses, and tells of a rich man whose ground brought forth plentifully and who resolved to pull down his barns and build greater to store his goods and tell his soul to take its ease, eat, drink, and be merry — but God said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee, and so is he that lays up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.

entries.old: Give to the one who begs; lend expecting nothing in return
entries.new: Jesus charges his hearers to give to him that asks and not to turn away from him who would borrow.

entries.old: Sell what you possess, give to the poor, and follow — store up treasure in heaven
entries.new: Jesus tells the rich young ruler that if he would be perfect he should go and sell what he has and give to the poor, and he shall have treasure in heaven, and come and follow him.

entries.old: Silences his opponents on the tax question — give to Caesar what bears his image, and to God what bears his
entries.new: Jesus, asked whether it is lawful to give tribute to Caesar, calls his questioners hypocrites, asks for the tribute money, and seeing Caesar's image and superscription tells them to render unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's and unto God the things that are God's.

entries.old: The parable of the talents / minas — faithful stewardship multiplies what is given; unfaithfulness forfeits it
entries.new: Jesus tells of a man traveling into a far country who delivers his goods to his servants — five talents to one, two to another, one to another, each according to his ability — and on his return commends the servants who traded and doubled what they were given as good and faithful, but condemns the servant who hid his lord's talent in the earth as wicked and slothful, taking that talent from him and casting the unprofitable servant into outer darkness, declaring that to everyone who has shall be given but from him who has not shall be taken away even that which he has.

entries.old: The widow's offering — she gave all she had out of poverty; it is more blessed to give than to receive
entries.new: Jesus says that the poor widow has cast more into the treasury than all the others, for they cast in of their abundance but she of her want cast in all that she had, even all her living.

entries.old: The dishonest manager — use worldly wealth wisely; one faithful in little is faithful in much
entries.new: Jesus tells of a steward accused of wasting his lord's goods who, about to be put out of his stewardship, calls in his lord's debtors and reduces their bills to make friends for himself, and the lord commends the unjust steward for acting wisely; he charges his hearers to make friends for themselves by the mammon of unrighteousness, declares that he who is faithful in the least is faithful also in much and he who is unjust in the least is unjust also in much, and says no servant can serve two masters — they cannot serve God and mammon.

entries.old: The rich man feasts while Lazarus lies at his gate — in the afterlife their positions are reversed; a great chasm is fixed
entries.new: Jesus tells of a rich man clothed in purple and fine linen who fared sumptuously every day and a beggar named Lazarus laid at his gate full of sores; when both died, Lazarus was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom while the rich man in hell lifted up his eyes in torments, and Abraham told him that in his lifetime he received his good things and Lazarus evil things but now he is comforted and the rich man tormented, and that between them a great gulf is fixed which none can pass.

entries.old: If they do not hear Moses and the Prophets, they will not be convinced even if someone rises from the dead
entries.new: Jesus, in the words of Abraham to the rich man, declares that if they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded though one rose from the dead.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Blessing on the Poor and Woe to the Rich
entries.old: Blessed are the poor — the kingdom of God is theirs; blessed are those who hunger; the poor have good news preached to them
entries.new: Jesus blesses the poor, declaring that theirs is the kingdom of God, and blesses those who hunger now, for they shall be filled, and those who weep now, for they shall laugh, but pronounces woe when all men speak well of his hearers, for so did their fathers to the false prophets.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Blessing on the Poor and Woe to the Rich
entries.old: Pronounces woe on the rich, full, and those who laugh now — they have already received their reward
entries.new: Jesus pronounces woe on the rich, for they have received their consolation, and on those that are full, for they shall hunger, and on those that laugh now, for they shall mourn and weep.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Judgment of the Nations — Sheep and Goats
entries.old: The Son of Man separates all nations as a shepherd separates sheep from goats — those who served the hungry, thirsty, stranger, naked, sick, and imprisoned served him
entries.new: Jesus describes the Son of man coming in his glory with all the holy angels and sitting upon the throne of his glory, before whom all nations are gathered and separated as a shepherd divides his sheep from the goats; the King bids those on his right to inherit the kingdom prepared from the foundation of the world because they fed him when hungry, gave him drink when thirsty, took him in as a stranger, clothed him, and visited him when sick and in prison, declaring that what was done unto one of the least of his brethren was done unto him, while those on his left are sent into everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels for failing to do these things, going away into everlasting punishment but the righteous into life eternal.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Judgment of the Nations — Sheep and Goats
entries.old: Whatever was done for the least of these was done for him; whatever was not done for the least was not done for him
entries.new: Jesus declares that whatever was done for one of the least of his brethren was done for him, and whatever was not done for the least was not done for him.

entries.old: Blessed are the merciful — they shall receive mercy; I desire mercy, not sacrifice
entries.new: Jesus blesses the merciful, declaring that they shall obtain mercy, and elsewhere says he desires mercy and not sacrifice.

entries.old: Has compassion on the crowd that has gone three days without food and refuses to send them away hungry
entries.new: Jesus says he has compassion on the multitude because they have continued with him three days and have nothing to eat, and that he will not send them away fasting lest they faint in the way.

entries.old: Stops for the two blind men outside Jericho and asks what they want him to do
entries.new: Jesus asks the two blind men what they would have him do for them.

entries.old: You neglect justice and the love of God — these ought to have been practiced without neglecting the others
entries.new: Jesus pronounces woe on the Pharisees who tithe mint, rue, and every herb yet neglect judgment and the love of God, saying these ought to have been done without leaving the others undone.

entries.old: The Good Samaritan — the one who showed mercy is the true neighbor; go and do likewise
entries.new: Jesus tells of a certain man going down from Jerusalem to Jericho who falls among thieves and is left half dead, passed by first a priest and then a Levite, until a certain Samaritan comes where he is, has compassion, binds his wounds with oil and wine, sets him on his own beast, brings him to an inn and pays the host to take care of him, and then asks which of the three was neighbor to the man who fell among the thieves, charging his hearer to go and do likewise.

entries.old: Sends ten lepers to show themselves to the priests — they are cleansed as they go
entries.new: Jesus sends the ten lepers to go and show themselves unto the priests.

entries.old: Notes that only the Samaritan among the ten cleansed lepers returned to give glory to God
entries.new: Jesus asks where the other nine are, noting that none returned to give glory to God save the one stranger, the Samaritan.

entries.old: Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men — come, follow me
entries.new: Jesus calls his first disciples to follow him, promising to make them fishers of men.

entries.old: Foxes have holes and birds have nests — the Son of Man has no place to lay his head; let the dead bury their own dead
entries.new: Jesus warns a would-be follower that the foxes have holes and the birds of the air have nests but the Son of man has nowhere to lay his head, and tells another to follow him and let the dead bury their dead.

entries.old: Calls Matthew the tax collector from his booth — Follow me
entries.new: Jesus calls Matthew the tax collector from his receipt of custom with the words, follow me.

entries.old: Redefines family — who is my mother and brethren? Behold my mother and my brethren — those who do God's will
entries.new: Jesus asks who is his mother and his brethren, and pointing to his disciples declares that those who do the will of his Father are his mother and brothers.

entries.old: Follow me — Jesus calls Levi the tax collector to leave his post and become a disciple
entries.new: Jesus calls Levi from the receipt of custom with the words, follow me.

entries.old: Calls the returning apostles to withdraw with him to a quiet place and rest
entries.new: Jesus calls the returning apostles to come apart with him into a desert place and rest a while.

entries.old: Tells Peter to put out into deep water and let down the nets for the miraculous catch
entries.new: Jesus tells Peter to launch out into the deep and let down his nets for a draught.

entries.old: Calls Peter from his nets — from now on he will catch people
entries.new: Jesus tells Peter to fear not, for from henceforth he shall catch men.

entries.old: Follow me — Jesus calls Levi the publican from the receipt of custom
entries.new: Jesus calls Levi the publican from the receipt of custom with the words, follow me.

entries.old: No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom
entries.new: Jesus declares that no man, having put his hand to the plough and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.

entries.old: Tells the anxious Martha that Mary has chosen the one needful thing, and it will not be taken from her
entries.new: Jesus tells the anxious Martha that she is careful and troubled about many things, but one thing is needful, and Mary has chosen that good part which shall not be taken away from her.

entries.old: He asks the first disciples what they seek and invites them to come and see where he dwells
entries.new: Jesus asks the first disciples what they seek and invites them to come and see where he dwells.

entries.old: He renames Simon son of Jonah as Cephas, meaning a stone, marking him with a new identity
entries.new: Jesus names Simon the son of Jona and declares that he shall be called Cephas.

entries.old: He reminds the twelve that he has chosen them, yet one of them is a devil
entries.new: Jesus reminds the twelve that he has chosen them, and yet one of them is a devil.

entries.old: He calls the disciples to go back into Judaea again despite the danger awaiting him there.
entries.new: Jesus calls his disciples to go with him into Judaea again.

entries.old: Where he goes Peter cannot follow now, but shall follow afterwards.
entries.new: Jesus tells Peter that whither he goes he cannot follow him now, but he shall follow him afterwards.

entries.old: Three times asks Peter "Do you love me?" — feed my lambs, tend my sheep, feed my sheep; predicts his martyrdom and calls him to follow
entries.new: Jesus three times asks Simon son of Jonas if he loves him, charging him to feed his lambs and feed his sheep, foretells that when he is old another shall gird him and carry him where he would not, and calls him to follow.

entries.old: Anyone who would follow must deny himself, take up his cross daily, and follow — the cost is total self-surrender
entries.new: Jesus declares that if any man will come after him, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow him.

entries.old: Whoever saves his life will lose it — whoever loses it for his sake will find it; what profits a man to gain the world and forfeit his soul?
entries.new: Jesus says that whoever will save his life shall lose it, and whoever loses his life for his sake shall find it, and asks what a man is profited if he gains the whole world and loses his own soul, or what a man shall give in exchange for his soul.

entries.old: Those who leave family or possessions for the kingdom will receive many times more, with eternal life
entries.new: Jesus declares that everyone who has forsaken houses or brethren or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or lands for his name's sake shall receive an hundredfold and shall inherit everlasting life.

entries.old: Confronts shallow disciples — why call him Lord but ignore his commands?
entries.new: Jesus asks why his hearers call him Lord, Lord, and do not the things which he says.

entries.old: Rebukes James and John for wanting to call fire on the Samaritans — he came to save lives, not destroy them
entries.new: Jesus rebukes James and John, telling them they know not what manner of spirit they are of, for the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives but to save them.

entries.old: Anyone who does not renounce family, possessions, and even his own life cannot be a disciple
entries.new: Jesus declares that if any man come to him and hate not his father and mother and wife and children and brethren and sisters, and his own life also, he cannot be his disciple, and that whoever forsakes not all that he has cannot be his disciple.

entries.old: The tower builder and the king going to war — count the cost before you begin
entries.new: Jesus likens the would-be disciple to a man intending to build a tower who first sits down and counts the cost lest he be unable to finish and be mocked, and to a king going to war who first considers whether with ten thousand he can meet one coming with twenty thousand or else sends an embassy desiring conditions of peace, and declares that whoever forsakes not all that he has cannot be his disciple.

entries.old: He asks the twelve whether they also will go away
entries.new: Jesus asks the twelve whether they also will go away.

entries.old: Defines true discipleship as continuing in his word
entries.new: Jesus declares that if his hearers continue in his word, then are they his disciples indeed.

entries.old: A good tree bears good fruit; a bad tree cannot — by their fruits you shall know them; every fruitless tree is cut down
entries.new: Jesus teaches that every good tree brings forth good fruit but a corrupt tree brings forth evil fruit, that a good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit nor a corrupt tree good fruit, that every tree that brings not forth good fruit is hewn down and cast into the fire, and that by their fruits they shall be known.

entries.old: Teaches that those who lose their life for him keep it — and even with a troubled soul, he chose this hour to glorify the Father
entries.new: Jesus declares that he who loves his life shall lose it and he who hates his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal, that if any man serve him let him follow him and where he is there shall his servant also be, and prays that though his soul is troubled, the Father glorify his name, for this cause he came unto this hour.

entries.old: He who abides in him bears much fruit — apart from him you can do nothing; the Father is glorified by much fruit
entries.new: Jesus declares that he is the vine and his hearers are the branches, that he who abides in him and he in him brings forth much fruit, for without him they can do nothing, and that the Father is glorified that they bear much fruit and so be his disciples.

entries.old: He chose them to go and bear fruit that abides; if his words abide in them, they may ask whatever they wish
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples that if they abide in him and his words abide in them they shall ask what they will and it shall be done unto them, and that he has chosen and ordained them to go and bring forth fruit that shall remain, so that whatsoever they ask of the Father in his name he may give it them.

entries.old: Answers Satan's first temptation by quoting Deuteronomy — man does not live by bread alone
entries.new: Jesus answers the tempter by declaring that it is written, man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.

entries.old: Refuses to test God by quoting Deuteronomy — do not put the Lord your God to the test
entries.new: Jesus answers the tempter that it is written again, thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.

entries.old: Commands Satan to leave — worship the Lord your God and serve him only
entries.new: Jesus commands Satan to depart, declaring that it is written, thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.

entries.old: Answers the bread temptation in Luke's account by citing Deuteronomy
entries.new: Jesus answers the tempter in Luke's account that it is written, man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.

entries.old: Rebukes Satan and quotes the command to worship and serve God alone
entries.new: Jesus rebukes Satan, telling him to get behind, for it is written that thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.

entries.old: Refuses the temple-pinnacle temptation — do not put the Lord your God to the test
entries.new: Jesus answers that it is said, thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.

entries.old: Blessed are those persecuted for righteousness — blessed when people revile and persecute; rejoice, for great is the reward in heaven
entries.new: Jesus blesses those who are persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven, and pronounces blessed his hearers when men shall revile and persecute them and say all manner of evil against them falsely for his sake, charging them to rejoice and be exceeding glad, for great is their reward in heaven, since so persecuted they the prophets which were before them.

entries.old: Notes the rejection at Nazareth — a prophet is honored everywhere except his hometown
entries.new: Jesus says that a prophet is not without honour, save in his own country and in his own house.

entries.old: Notes that a prophet is dishonored only by his hometown, his relatives, and his own household
entries.new: Jesus says that a prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.

entries.old: If the world hates them they should know it hated him first; because they are not of the world but chosen out of it, the world hates them.
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples that if the world hate them, they know that it hated him before it hated them, and that because they are not of the world but he has chosen them out of the world, therefore the world hateth them.

entries.old: If they persecuted him, they will persecute his followers — a servant is not greater than his master; you will be hated by all for his name
entries.new: Jesus charges the disciples to remember the word he said unto them, that the servant is not greater than his lord, and that if they have persecuted him they will also persecute them, and if they have kept his saying they will keep theirs also.

entries.old: Tells the disciples the world will persecute them because it has rejected him and the Father — fulfilling the scripture 'they hated me without cause'
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples that the world will do all these things unto them for his name's sake because they know not him that sent him, and that had he not come and spoken and done among them the works which none other man did, they had not had sin, but now they have no cloke for their sin and have both seen and hated him and the Father, that the word might be fulfilled which is written in their law, they hated me without a cause.

entries.old: They will be put out of synagogues; the hour is coming when killing them will seem like worship of God
entries.new: Jesus warns that they shall put his disciples out of the synagogues, and that the time cometh when whosoever killeth them will think that he doeth God service.

entries.old: Do not fear those who kill the body but not the soul — fear him who can destroy both; not a hair of your head will perish
entries.new: Jesus charges his disciples to fear not them which kill the body but are not able to kill the soul, but rather to fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.

entries.old: Has warned the disciples in advance so they will not stumble when persecution comes
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples that these things he has spoken unto them, that they should not be offended.

entries.old: Forewarns the disciples of persecution — sorrow fills their hearts now, but he is going to the Father who sent him
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples that the world will do these things unto them because they have not known the Father nor him, and that he has told them so that when the time shall come they may remember he told them, saying that he did not say these things at the beginning because he was with them, but now he goes his way to him that sent him, and because he has said these things sorrow hath filled their heart.

entries.old: Promises their grief will turn to joy like a mother's after birth — a joy no one will take from them
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples that a little while and they shall not see him, and again a little while and they shall see him, and that they shall weep and lament while the world rejoices, but their sorrow shall be turned into joy as a woman in travail forgets her anguish for joy that a man is born into the world, promising that he will see them again and their heart shall rejoice and their joy no man taketh from them.

entries.old: Warns the disciples they will scatter and abandon him — yet he is not alone because the Father is with him
entries.new: Jesus asks the disciples whether they now believe, and declares that the hour cometh, yea is now come, when they shall be scattered every man to his own and shall leave him alone, yet he is not alone because the Father is with him.

entries.old: In the world they will have tribulation — but take heart; he has overcome the world; by endurance they will gain their lives
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples that these things he has spoken unto them that in him they might have peace, and that in the world they shall have tribulation, but charges them to be of good cheer, for he has overcome the world.

entries.old: Answers Paul's plea about the thorn — his grace is sufficient and his strength is perfected in weakness
entries.new: Jesus answers that his grace is sufficient for him, for his strength is made perfect in weakness.

entries.old: Anyone who would follow must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow — whoever saves his life will lose it; whoever loses it for his sake will save it
entries.new: Jesus says that if any man will come after him, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow him, for whosoever will save his life shall lose it and whosoever will lose his life for his sake shall find it, and declares that there be some standing there which shall not taste of death till they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.

entries.old: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world and forfeit his soul?
entries.new: Jesus asks what is a man profited if he shall gain the whole world and lose his own soul, or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Seven Woes to Scribes and Pharisees (Matthew 23)
entries.old: Woe: they shut the kingdom of heaven in people's faces — they neither enter nor let others in
entries.new: Jesus pronounces woe upon the scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for shutting up the kingdom of heaven against men, neither going in themselves nor suffering those who are entering to go in.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Seven Woes to Scribes and Pharisees (Matthew 23)
entries.old: Woe: They devour widows' houses and make long prayers for a show
entries.new: Jesus pronounces woe upon the scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for devouring widows' houses and for a pretence making long prayer, declaring that they shall receive the greater damnation.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Seven Woes to Scribes and Pharisees (Matthew 23)
entries.old: Woe: they travel far to make one convert, then make him twice the child of hell
entries.new: Jesus pronounces woe upon the scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, make him twofold more the child of hell than themselves.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Seven Woes to Scribes and Pharisees (Matthew 23)
entries.old: Woe: blind guides who strain out a gnat but swallow a camel — neglecting what actually sanctifies
entries.new: Jesus pronounces woe upon the blind guides who say swearing by the temple is nothing but swearing by the gold of the temple binds, and swearing by the altar is nothing but swearing by the gift binds, asking which is greater — the gold or the temple that sanctifies it, the gift or the altar that sanctifies it — and condemns them as hypocrites who tithe mint and anise and cummin yet have omitted the weightier matters of the law: judgment, mercy, and faith, straining at a gnat and swallowing a camel.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Seven Woes to Scribes and Pharisees (Matthew 23)
entries.old: Woe: they tithe mint and dill but neglect justice, mercy, and faithfulness
entries.new: Jesus pronounces woe upon the scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin yet have omitted the weightier matters of the law — judgment, mercy, and faith — saying these ought they to have done and not to leave the other undone.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Seven Woes to Scribes and Pharisees (Matthew 23)
entries.old: Woe: they clean the outside of the cup while inside is greed and self-indulgence
entries.new: Jesus pronounces woe upon the scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who make clean the outside of the cup and platter while within they are full of extortion and excess, charging the blind Pharisee to cleanse first that which is within so that the outside may be clean also.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Seven Woes to Scribes and Pharisees (Matthew 23)
