entries.old: Woe: they are like whitewashed tombs — beautiful outside, full of dead bones within
entries.new: Jesus pronounces woe upon the scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, likening them to whited sepulchres which appear beautiful outward but within are full of dead men's bones and all uncleanness, so that they outwardly appear righteous unto men while within being full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Seven Woes to Scribes and Pharisees (Matthew 23)
entries.old: Woe: they build tombs for prophets while being sons of those who killed them; brood of vipers — how will they escape hell?
entries.new: Jesus pronounces woe upon the scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who build the tombs of the prophets and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous while saying that had they lived in the days of their fathers they would not have shared in the prophets' blood, calling them witnesses against themselves as children of those who killed the prophets, and demanding of them, ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Seven Woes to Scribes and Pharisees (Matthew 23)
entries.old: Pronounces woe on the Pharisees who crave the best seats and respectful greetings in public
entries.new: Jesus pronounces woe upon the Pharisees, for they love the uppermost seats in the synagogues and greetings in the markets.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Seven Woes to Scribes and Pharisees (Matthew 23)
entries.old: Pronounces woe on the lawyers who pile heavy burdens on others but won't lift a finger to carry them
entries.new: Jesus pronounces woe upon the lawyers, for they lade men with burdens grievous to be borne yet themselves touch not the burdens with one of their fingers.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Seven Woes to Scribes and Pharisees (Matthew 23)
entries.old: Pronounces woe on lawyers who take away the key of knowledge — blocking the way and refusing to enter themselves
entries.new: Jesus declares that the wisdom of God says, I will send them prophets and apostles, some of whom they shall slay and persecute, so that the blood of all the prophets shed from the foundation of the world — from Abel to Zacharias who perished between the altar and the temple — shall be required of this generation, and he pronounces woe upon the lawyers who have taken away the key of knowledge, neither entering in themselves nor suffering those who were entering to go in.

entries.old: Compares the fickle generation to children in the marketplace — they rejected both John's fasting and his own feasting
entries.new: Jesus likens this generation to children sitting in the markets calling to their fellows, We have piped unto you and ye have not danced, we have mourned unto you and ye have not lamented, for John came neither eating nor drinking and they say he has a devil, and the Son of man comes eating and drinking and they call him a gluttonous man and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners — but wisdom is justified of her children.

entries.old: Refuses the sign-seekers — only the sign of Jonah will be given to this evil generation
entries.new: Jesus declares that an evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, and that no sign shall be given to it but the sign of the prophet Jonas.

entries.old: These people honor him with their lips but their hearts are far from him — in vain they worship, teaching human traditions
entries.new: Jesus says of the people that they draw nigh unto him with their mouth and honor him with their lips while their heart is far from him, and that in vain they worship him, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.

entries.old: It is not what goes into a person that defiles him — what defiles comes from within: evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft, murder, slander, arrogance
entries.new: Jesus teaches that not that which goes into the mouth defiles a man but that which comes out of the mouth, for the things that proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart and defile the man — for out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, and blasphemies.

entries.old: Repeats the rebuke — only the sign of Jonah will be given to this wicked generation
entries.new: Jesus declares that a wicked and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, and that no sign shall be given unto it but the sign of the prophet Jonas.

entries.old: Curses the fruitless fig tree — it will never bear fruit again
entries.new: Jesus speaks to the fruitless fig tree, charging that no fruit grow on it henceforward for ever.

entries.old: Tests the Syrophoenician woman — the children's bread is not for the dogs
entries.new: Jesus tells the Syrophoenician woman to let the children first be filled, for it is not meet to take the children's bread and cast it unto the dogs.

entries.old: The Pharisee and the tax collector — self-righteousness condemned; humility justified
entries.new: Jesus tells of two men who go up to the temple to pray — a Pharisee who stands and thanks God that he is not as other men, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as the publican, recounting his fasts and tithes, and a publican who stands afar off, will not lift up his eyes to heaven, but smites his breast saying, God be merciful to me a sinner — and declares that this man went down to his house justified rather than the other, for everyone who exalts himself shall be abased and he who humbles himself shall be exalted.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Traditions of Men Versus God's Commands
entries.old: They have made void the word of God for the sake of tradition — Isaiah prophesied rightly about them
entries.new: Jesus tells the Pharisees that they have made the commandment of God of none effect by their tradition, calling them hypocrites of whom Esaias well prophesied.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Traditions of Men Versus God's Commands
entries.old: Accuses the Pharisees of setting aside God's command to keep human traditions like ritual washings
entries.new: Jesus charges the Pharisees with laying aside the commandment of God to hold the tradition of men, such as the washing of pots and cups and many other such like things.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Traditions of Men Versus God's Commands
entries.old: They reject God's commands to keep their own traditions — the tradition of Corban nullifies the command to honor parents
entries.new: Jesus tells the Pharisees that they full well reject the commandment of God to keep their own tradition, citing how Moses commanded to honor father and mother and that whoso curses father or mother let him die the death, but they say that if a man tells his father or mother that any benefit they would have received is Corban — a gift — he is freed from helping them, thereby making the word of God of none effect through their tradition.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Traditions of Men Versus God's Commands
entries.old: Calls the crowd to listen carefully as he teaches what truly defiles a person
entries.new: Jesus calls the multitude to hearken unto him every one and to understand.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Traditions of Men Versus God's Commands
entries.old: Explains to the disciples that what enters from outside cannot defile — defilement comes from within
entries.new: Jesus explains to the disciples that whatever thing from without enters into the man cannot defile him because it enters not into his heart but into the belly and goes out into the draught, purging all meats, but that which comes out of the man — that defiles the man.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Traditions of Men Versus God's Commands
entries.old: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man — the heart is the source of moral corruption
entries.new: Jesus declares that all these evil things come from within and defile the man.

entries.old: It is lawful to do good on the Sabbath — would you not rescue an animal or a child? This woman bound by Satan ought to be loosed
entries.new: Jesus asks what man among them, having one sheep that falls into a pit on the sabbath day, will not lay hold of it and lift it out, and reasons that since a man is much better than a sheep, it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.

entries.old: The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath — the Son of Man is Lord of it
entries.new: Jesus declares that the sabbath was made for man and not man for the sabbath, and that therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.

entries.old: Reminds the Pharisees that hungry David ate the showbread which only priests were permitted
entries.new: Jesus asks the Pharisees whether they have not read what David did when he was hungry, how he went into the house of God and took and ate the shewbread and gave also to those with him, which it was not lawful to eat but for the priests alone.

entries.old: Calls the man with the withered hand forward and asks if it is lawful to do good or save life on the Sabbath
entries.new: Jesus calls the man with the withered hand to rise up and stand forth in the midst, then asks his hearers whether it is lawful on the sabbath days to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it, before bidding the man to stretch forth his hand.

entries.old: Heals the bent-over woman in the synagogue — releases her from eighteen years of infirmity
entries.new: Jesus says to the bent-over woman in the synagogue, Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity.

entries.old: Calls the synagogue ruler a hypocrite — they all untie an ox or donkey to water it on the Sabbath
entries.new: Jesus calls the synagogue ruler a hypocrite, asking does not each of them on the sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the stall and lead him away to watering.

entries.old: Asks the lawyers and Pharisees whether Sabbath healing is lawful before healing the man with dropsy
entries.new: Jesus asks the lawyers and Pharisees whether it is lawful to heal on the sabbath day.

entries.old: He defends his Sabbath healing by appealing to the lawful practice of circumcision on the Sabbath, asking why they are angry that he made a man whole
entries.new: Jesus says that he has done one work and they all marvel, and reasons that since Moses gave them circumcision and they circumcise a man on the sabbath day so that the law of Moses should not be broken, they should not be angry at him because he has made a man every whit whole on the sabbath day.

entries.old: Warns the disciples that every plant the Father did not plant will be uprooted
entries.new: Jesus warns that every plant which his heavenly Father has not planted shall be rooted up.

entries.old: Concludes the teaching on defilement — these are the things that defile a man, but eating with unwashen hands does not
entries.new: Jesus concludes that these are the things which defile a man, but to eat with unwashen hands defiles not a man.

entries.old: Cleanses the temple — declares it the house of prayer that they have made into a robbers' den
entries.new: Jesus declares in the temple that it is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer, but they have made it a den of thieves.

entries.old: The scribes and Pharisees sit on Moses's seat — do what they say but not what they do; they burden others but will not lift a finger
entries.new: Jesus says that the scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat, charging his hearers to observe and do whatsoever they bid but not to do after their works, for they say and do not, binding heavy and grievous burdens upon men's shoulders while they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.

entries.old: They do all their deeds to be seen — they love places of honor, greetings in marketplaces, and titles
entries.new: Jesus says that the scribes and Pharisees do all their works to be seen of men, making broad their phylacteries and enlarging the borders of their garments, loving the uppermost rooms at feasts, the chief seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets, and to be called of men Rabbi, Rabbi — and charges his hearers not to be called Rabbi nor master, for one is their Master, even Christ, and all are brethren.

entries.old: Declares he sends prophets and wise men whom they will kill — pronounces the Jerusalem lament: how often would he have gathered her children, but they were not willing
entries.new: Jesus declares that he sends them prophets and wise men and scribes, of whom some they shall kill and crucify and others scourge in their synagogues and persecute from city to city, so that upon them shall come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth from Abel to Zacharias slain between the temple and the altar, and laments, O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that kills the prophets and stones those sent unto her, how often would he have gathered her children as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, and they would not.

entries.old: Curses the unfruitful fig tree as a sign against barren, pretentious religion
entries.new: Jesus speaks to the unfruitful fig tree, charging that no man eat fruit of it hereafter for ever.

entries.old: Cleanses the temple, citing Isaiah — God's house for all nations has been turned into a robbers' den
entries.new: Jesus asks in the temple, Is it not written, My house shall be called of all nations the house of prayer — but ye have made it a den of thieves.

entries.old: Counters the authority challenge with his own question — was John's baptism from heaven or from men?
entries.new: Jesus tells the chief priests that he will ask them one question, and if they answer he will tell them by what authority he does these things, asking whether the baptism of John was from heaven or of men.

entries.old: Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things — Jesus refuses the chief priests' challenge
entries.new: Jesus tells the chief priests, neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.

entries.old: Exposes the Pharisees who justify themselves before men — what they prize, God despises
entries.new: Jesus tells the Pharisees that they justify themselves before men but God knows their hearts, for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.

entries.old: Cleanses the temple in Luke's account — God's house of prayer turned into a robbers' den
entries.new: Jesus declares in the temple that it is written, My house is the house of prayer, but they have made it a den of thieves.

entries.old: Exposes that they reject him while seeking human glory — and Moses, whom they trust, accuses them
entries.new: Jesus tells the religious leaders that he receives not honor from men but knows that they have not the love of God in them, that he is come in his Father's name and they receive him not while if another comes in his own name him they will receive, asking how they can believe who receive honor one of another and seek not the honor that comes from God only — and declares that he need not accuse them to the Father, for there is one that accuses them, even Moses, in whom they trust.

entries.old: Tells the religious leaders their father is the devil — a murderer and liar — not Abraham, since they reject his truth
entries.new: Jesus tells the religious leaders that though he knows they are Abraham's seed, they seek to kill him because his word has no place in them, and that if they were Abraham's children they would do the works of Abraham — but they do the deeds of their father, who is the devil, a murderer from the beginning who abode not in the truth and is a liar and the father of it, and because he tells them the truth they believe him not, for he that is of God hears God's words, and they hear them not because they are not of God.

entries.old: On this rock he will build his church — the gates of hell shall not prevail; he gives the keys of the kingdom
entries.new: Jesus tells Peter that upon this rock he will build his church and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it, and gives him the keys of the kingdom of heaven so that whatsoever he binds on earth shall be bound in heaven and whatsoever he looses on earth shall be loosed in heaven.

entries.old: Grants the disciples authority to bind and loose — heaven will ratify their decisions
entries.new: Jesus grants the disciples authority to bind and loose, declaring that whatsoever they bind on earth shall be bound in heaven and whatsoever they loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.

entries.old: Where two or three are gathered in his name, there he is among them; if two agree about anything they ask, it will be done
entries.new: Jesus says that if two of them agree on earth as touching anything they ask, it shall be done by his Father in heaven, for where two or three are gathered together in his name there he is in the midst of them.

entries.old: Tells the disciples not to stop the unknown exorcist working in his name — whoever is not against us is for us
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples not to forbid the unknown man working a miracle in his name, for no man can do so and lightly speak evil of him, and whoever is not against them is on their part.

entries.old: Commissions the eleven, and all followers of Christ, to make disciples of all nations
entries.new: Jesus declares that all power in heaven and earth has been given to him and charges the eleven to go and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost, and teaching them to observe all that he has commanded, with the promise that he is with them always, even unto the end of the world.

entries.old: You will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you — be my witnesses in Jerusalem, Judaea, Samaria, and to the ends of the earth
entries.new: Jesus tells the apostles that they shall receive power after the Holy Ghost has come upon them and shall be his witnesses in Jerusalem, in all Judaea and Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Instructions for the Twelve and the Seventy
entries.old: Take no bag, no purse — the worker deserves his wages; if a town welcomes, stay; if not, shake the dust off your feet
entries.new: Jesus charges the twelve to go not among the Gentiles or Samaritans but to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, to provide neither gold nor silver nor extra clothing for the workman is worthy of his meat, to lodge with whoever is worthy in each town and to shake the dust from their feet where they are not received, to beware of men who will deliver them to councils and synagogues, and to know that whoever loses his life for his sake shall find it and whoever receives them receives him and the one who sent him.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Instructions for the Twelve and the Seventy
entries.old: Go and proclaim: the kingdom of heaven is at hand; heal the sick, raise the dead, cast out demons — freely give
entries.new: Jesus sends the twelve forth to preach that the kingdom of heaven is at hand, to heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, and cast out devils, charging them that as they have freely received they shall freely give.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Instructions for the Twelve and the Seventy
entries.old: Behold, he sends them as sheep among wolves — be wise as serpents and innocent as doves
entries.new: Jesus tells the twelve that he sends them forth as sheep in the midst of wolves and charges them therefore to be wise as serpents and harmless as doves.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Instructions for the Twelve and the Seventy
entries.old: Tells the disciples to move on to neighboring towns — preaching is the purpose of his coming
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples that they must go into the next towns so that he may preach there also, for that is why he came forth.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Instructions for the Twelve and the Seventy
entries.old: Receives the seventy back joyfully — saw Satan fall like lightning, but they should rejoice their names are in heaven
entries.new: Jesus tells the returning seventy that he beheld Satan fall as lightning from heaven and that he gives them power to tread on serpents and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy, charging them not to rejoice that the spirits are subject to them but rather that their names are written in heaven, and he thanks the Father for hiding these things from the wise and revealing them unto babes.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Visions and Commissions to the Apostles
entries.old: Confronts Saul on the Damascus road — 'I am Jesus whom you persecute' — and sends him into the city for further instructions
entries.new: Jesus calls out to Saul on the Damascus road, asking why he persecutes him and declaring himself to be Jesus whom Saul persecutes, and tells him it is hard to kick against the pricks and to arise and go into the city where he will be told what he must do.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Visions and Commissions to the Apostles
entries.old: In a vision sends Ananias to Saul — a chosen instrument to carry his name before Gentiles, kings, and Israel
entries.new: Jesus calls Ananias in a vision and sends him to the street called Straight to lay hands on Saul of Tarsus that he may receive his sight, declaring that Saul is a chosen vessel to bear his name before the Gentiles, kings, and the children of Israel, and that he will show him how great things he must suffer for his name's sake.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Visions and Commissions to the Apostles
entries.old: Tells Peter in a vision to rise, kill, and eat — what God has made clean must not be called common
entries.new: Jesus tells Peter in a vision to rise, kill, and eat from the creatures let down before him, and when Peter refuses what is common or unclean, declares that what God has cleansed Peter must not call common.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Visions and Commissions to the Apostles
entries.old: Appears to Paul in Corinth — speak, do not fear, for many in this city belong to him and no one will harm him
entries.new: Jesus tells Paul in a night vision at Corinth not to be afraid but to speak and hold not his peace, for he is with him and no man shall set on him to hurt him, because he has much people in that city.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Visions and Commissions to the Apostles
entries.old: Tells Paul in a temple trance to leave Jerusalem — they will not receive his testimony; he is sent to Gentiles far off
entries.new: Jesus tells Paul in a trance at the temple to make haste and depart quickly from Jerusalem, for they will not receive his testimony concerning him, and declares that he will send him far hence unto the Gentiles.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Visions and Commissions to the Apostles
entries.old: The Lord stands by Paul in his Jerusalem custody and encourages him, confirming that just as he has testified about him in Jerusalem he must also testify in Rome.
entries.new: Jesus stands by Paul in his Jerusalem custody and bids him be of good cheer, declaring that as he has testified of him in Jerusalem so must he also bear witness at Rome.

entries.old: The harvest is plentiful but the workers are few — pray earnestly to the Lord to send out laborers
entries.new: Jesus says that the harvest truly is plenteous but the labourers are few, and charges his disciples to pray the Lord of the harvest to send forth labourers into his harvest.

entries.old: No prophet is accepted in his own country — Elijah was sent to a widow of Sidon, and only Naaman the Syrian was cleansed
entries.new: Jesus declares in the Nazareth synagogue that no prophet is accepted in his own country, recalling that in the days of Elias many widows were in Israel during the famine yet he was sent only to a widow in Sarepta of Sidon, and many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus yet none were cleansed save Naaman the Syrian.

entries.old: Tells the crowd at Capernaum he must move on to preach the kingdom in other towns
entries.new: Jesus tells the crowd at Capernaum that he must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also, for to that end he was sent.

entries.old: Likens the fickle generation to children in the market — they reject both John's austerity and his own table fellowship
entries.new: Jesus likens the men of his generation to children sitting in the marketplace who complain that their fellows neither danced when they piped nor wept when they mourned, for John the Baptist came neither eating nor drinking and they said he had a devil, and the Son of man comes eating and drinking and they call him a gluttonous man and a winebibber, yet wisdom is justified of all her children.

entries.old: Sends the healed Gerasene demoniac home to tell what God has done for him
entries.new: Jesus sends the healed Gerasene demoniac back to his own house to show how great things God has done for him.

entries.old: Tells the disciples his food is to do the Father's will — the fields are ripe for harvest, sower and reaper rejoicing together
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples that his meat is to do the will of him that sent him and to finish his work, bidding them lift up their eyes and look on the fields already white for harvest, where the reaper receives wages and gathers fruit unto life eternal so that sower and reaper may rejoice together, and reminds them that he sent them to reap that whereon they bestowed no labour, for other men have laboured and they have entered into their labours.

entries.old: Tells the disciples they will bear witness — they have been with him from the beginning
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples that they also shall bear witness, because they have been with him from the beginning.

entries.old: What is whispered, proclaim on the housetops; do not fear those who kill the body — fear him who can destroy both soul and body
entries.new: Jesus charges the disciples to speak in the light what he tells them in darkness and to preach upon the housetops what they hear in the ear, and to fear not those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul, but rather him who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.

entries.old: Everyone who acknowledges him before men, he will acknowledge before the Father; whoever denies him, he will deny
entries.new: Jesus declares that whoever confesses him before men, he will also confess before his Father in heaven, but whoever denies him before men, he will also deny before his Father in heaven.

entries.old: They will be dragged before governors and kings — the gospel must first be proclaimed to all nations
entries.new: Jesus warns the disciples that they shall be brought before governors and kings for his sake as a testimony against them and the Gentiles.

entries.old: Brother will betray brother; they will be hated by all for his name's sake — he who endures to the end will be saved
entries.new: Jesus warns that brother shall deliver up brother to death and the father the child, and children shall rise against parents and cause them to be put to death, and that his disciples shall be hated of all men for his name's sake, but he that endures to the end shall be saved.

entries.old: Not a hair of your head will perish — by your endurance you will gain your lives
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples that not a hair of their head shall perish, and that in their patience they shall possess their souls.

entries.old: Foretells his crucifixion at Passover — after two days is the feast, and the Son of man is betrayed to be crucified
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples that after two days is the feast of the passover, and the Son of man is betrayed to be crucified.

entries.old: Defends the woman who anointed him — she has done a good work, pouring ointment for my burial, and shall be remembered wherever the gospel is preached
entries.new: Jesus defends the woman who poured ointment on him, saying she has wrought a good work upon him for his burial, and declares that wherever this gospel is preached in the whole world what she has done shall be told for a memorial of her.

entries.old: Sends two disciples to prepare the Passover meal at the appointed house
entries.new: Jesus sends his disciples into the city to a certain man with the message that the Master's time is at hand and he will keep the passover at his house with his disciples.

entries.old: Announces at the Last Supper that one of the Twelve will betray him
entries.new: Jesus declares to the Twelve at table that one of them shall betray him.

entries.old: Identifies the betrayer as the one who dips with him — better for that man if he had never been born
entries.new: Jesus says that the one who dips his hand with him in the dish shall betray him, that the Son of man goes as it is written of him but woe to that man by whom he is betrayed — it had been good for that man if he had not been born — and confirms to the questioner, Thou hast said.

entries.old: At the Last Supper Jesus institutes the bread and the cup — this is my body, this is my blood of the new testament shed for many for the remission of sins; he will not drink of the vine again until the kingdom of his Father.
entries.new: Jesus takes the bread and the cup at the supper, telling the disciples to take and eat for this is his body and to drink of it for this is his blood of the new testament shed for many for the remission of sins, and declares he will not drink henceforth of the fruit of the vine until that day when he drinks it new with them in his Father's kingdom.

entries.old: At the Last Supper Jesus institutes the Lord’s Supper — this is my body, this is my blood of the new testament shed for many for the remission of sins; he will not drink of the fruit of the vine again until the kingdom of God
entries.new: Jesus institutes the Lord's Supper, bidding the disciples to take and eat his body and to drink of the cup which is his blood of the new testament shed for many for the remission of sins, and pledges he will not drink of the fruit of the vine again until that day when he drinks it new with them in his Father's kingdom.

entries.old: Foretells the disciples' scattering, citing Zechariah — but pledges to meet them in Galilee after he rises
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples that all of them shall be offended because of him this night, citing the scripture that the shepherd shall be smitten and the sheep of the flock scattered abroad, but pledges that after he is risen again he will go before them into Galilee.

entries.old: Foretells Peter's three denials before the rooster crows that very night
entries.new: Jesus tells Peter that this very night, before the cock crows, he shall deny him three times.

entries.old: Tells the disciples he longed to share this Passover before his suffering — and will not eat it again until the kingdom comes
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples that with desire he has desired to eat this passover with them before he suffers, and says he will not eat of it again until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.

entries.old: At the Last Supper dispute over greatness, tells the disciples that gentile rulers lord over their subjects but among them the greatest must be as the youngest and the leader as one who serves
entries.new: Jesus says the kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them and those in authority are called benefactors, but charges his disciples that it shall not be so among them — he that is greatest must be as the younger, and he that is chief as he that serves.

entries.old: At table, asks who is greater — the one who reclines or the one who serves — and declares himself to be among them as one who serves
entries.new: Jesus asks which is greater, he that sits at meat or he that serves, and declares that he himself is among them as one who serves.

entries.old: At the Last Supper, commends the disciples for remaining with him through his trials and promises them thrones to judge the twelve tribes; warns Peter that Satan has asked to sift him but that he has prayed for Peter's faith to hold
entries.new: Jesus commends his disciples for having continued with him in his temptations and appoints unto them a kingdom as his Father has appointed unto him, that they may eat and drink at his table in his kingdom and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel; he warns Simon that Satan has desired to sift him as wheat, but that he has prayed for him that his faith fail not, and charges him when he is converted to strengthen his brethren.

entries.old: Calls the disciples in Gethsemane to stay alert and pray — the spirit is willing but the flesh is weak
entries.new: Jesus bids the disciples to sit while he goes and prays, telling them his soul is exceeding sorrowful even unto death and asking them to watch with him; he prays to the Father that if it be possible the cup might pass from him, yet not as he wills but as the Father wills, and again that if the cup may not pass except he drink it the Father's will be done; he rebukes them for not watching one hour, charging them to watch and pray that they enter not into temptation, for the spirit indeed is willing but the flesh is weak; and at last tells them to sleep on, for the hour is at hand and the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners — rise, let us be going, for he is at hand that betrays him.

entries.old: Greets Judas at the betrayal — friend, do what you came for
entries.new: Jesus greets Judas at the betrayal, asking, Friend, wherefore art thou come?

entries.old: Stops Peter's sword at his arrest — those who live by the sword die by it; the Scriptures must be fulfilled
entries.new: Jesus charges Peter to put up his sword, for all who take the sword shall perish with the sword; he says he could pray to his Father and be given more than twelve legions of angels, but asks how then the scriptures should be fulfilled that thus it must be; and to the arresting party he asks if they have come out as against a thief with swords and staves, though he sat daily teaching in the temple and they laid no hold on him — yet all this was done that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled.

entries.old: Confronts the arresting party — they come with swords as for a robber, though he taught openly daily in the temple
entries.new: Jesus asks the arresting party whether they have come out as against a thief with swords and staves to take him, noting that he was daily with them in the temple teaching and they took him not, but the scriptures must be fulfilled.

entries.old: Confronts Judas at his arrest — does he betray the Son of Man with a kiss?
entries.new: Jesus asks Judas whether he betrays the Son of man with a kiss.

entries.old: Going forth to those who came to arrest him, he asks, Whom do you seek?
entries.new: Jesus goes forth to those who came to arrest him and asks, Whom seek ye?

entries.old: At his arrest, twice declares 'I am he' — and the arresting party falls back to the ground at the words
entries.new: Jesus declares I am he to those who came to arrest him, asks again whom they seek, and tells them that since he has said he is the one, they should let his disciples go their way.

entries.old: He confirms to the high priest: I AM the Christ, the Son of God, coming on the clouds in power
entries.new: Jesus answers the high priest, Thou hast said, and declares that hereafter they shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power and coming in the clouds of heaven.

entries.old: Affirms before Pilate that he is the King of the Jews
entries.new: Jesus answers Pilate's question whether he is the King of the Jews with the words, Thou sayest.

entries.old: Tells the weeping women on the way to the cross to weep for themselves and their children, not for him
entries.new: Jesus tells the daughters of Jerusalem not to weep for him but for themselves and their children, for the days are coming when they shall say blessed are the barren and the wombs that never bare, and they shall begin to call to the mountains to fall on them and the hills to cover them; for if these things are done in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry?

entries.old: Tells the high priest he taught openly in synagogue and temple — those who heard him should be questioned
entries.new: Jesus tells the high priest that he spake openly to the world, ever taught in the synagogue and in the temple where the Jews resort, and said nothing in secret, and asks why he is questioned — let those who heard him be asked, for they know what he has said.

entries.old: If he has spoken evil, let the officer bear witness of the evil; but if he has spoken well, why is he struck?
entries.new: Jesus answers the officer who struck him, saying that if he has spoken evil let him bear witness of the evil, but if well, why is he smitten?

entries.old: He asks Pilate whether he says this of himself, or whether others have told him concerning Jesus.
entries.new: Jesus asks Pilate whether he says this thing of himself or whether others have told it him concerning Jesus.

entries.old: Tells Pilate his kingdom is not of this world — otherwise his servants would fight to prevent his arrest
entries.new: Jesus tells Pilate that his kingdom is not of this world, for if it were his servants would fight that he should not be delivered to the Jews, but his kingdom is not from hence.

entries.old: Before Pilate, declares he was born and came into the world to bear witness to the truth — everyone on the side of truth listens to him
entries.new: Jesus tells Pilate, Thou sayest that I am a king, and declares that to this end was he born and for this cause came he into the world, that he should bear witness unto the truth, and that everyone who is of the truth hears his voice.

entries.old: Pilate would have no power against him at all unless it were given from above; therefore the one who delivered him to Pilate has the greater sin.
entries.new: Jesus tells Pilate that he could have no power against him at all unless it were given him from above, and therefore the one who delivered him to Pilate has the greater sin.

entries.old: At the ninth hour Jesus cries out with a loud voice the opening words of Psalm 22 — 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?' — giving voice to the full weight of divine abandonment he bears as the sin-bearer on the cross.
entries.new: At the ninth hour Jesus cries out with a loud voice, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani — My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?

entries.old: From the cross Jesus prays for those who are crucifying him, asking the Father to forgive them on the ground that they do not understand what they are doing — extending mercy to his executioners at the very moment of his suffering.
entries.new: From the cross Jesus prays, Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.

entries.old: Jesus assures the repentant criminal crucified beside him that on that very day he will be with him in paradise, offering immediate salvation to one who turns to him in his final moments.
entries.new: Jesus tells the repentant criminal crucified beside him, Verily I say unto thee, today shalt thou be with me in paradise.

entries.old: With a loud voice Jesus entrusts his spirit to the Father in the words of Psalm 31:5, committing himself to God's care as he breathes his last and demonstrating that his death is a voluntary, trusting surrender into the Father's hands.
entries.new: With a loud voice Jesus cries, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit.

entries.old: From the cross Jesus entrusts his mother to the care of the beloved disciple, saying to her 'Woman, behold your son' and to the disciple 'Behold your mother,' establishing a new family bond at the moment of his death.
entries.new: From the cross Jesus says to his mother, Woman, behold thy son, and to the beloved disciple, Behold thy mother.

entries.old: Jesus declares 'I thirst' from the cross, fulfilling Scripture and expressing the full physical humanity of the Son of God in his atoning suffering.
entries.new: Jesus says from the cross, I thirst.

entries.old: Jesus cries out 'It is finished' (tetelestai) as his final public word before death, declaring the complete accomplishment of his atoning work and the full discharge of every obligation his mission required.
entries.new: Jesus cries out from the cross, It is finished.

entries.old: Joins the two disciples on the Emmaus road and asks what they are discussing so sadly
entries.new: Jesus joins the two disciples on the Emmaus road and asks what manner of communications they have one to another as they walk, and why they are sad.

entries.old: What things? — Jesus draws out the Emmaus disciples' account of Jesus of Nazareth
entries.new: Jesus, walking with the Emmaus disciples, simply asks what things, drawing out their account of Jesus of Nazareth.

entries.old: Rebukes the Emmaus disciples for being slow to believe the prophets — the Christ had to suffer to enter glory
entries.new: Jesus calls the two disciples fools and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken, asking whether the Christ ought not to have suffered these things and so entered into his glory.

entries.old: Greets the gathered disciples on resurrection evening — peace to you
entries.new: Jesus appears among the gathered disciples on the resurrection evening and greets them, saying peace be unto you.

entries.old: Calms the disciples by showing his hands and feet — a spirit has no flesh, and Moses, Prophets, and Psalms speak of him
entries.new: Jesus asks the disciples why they are troubled and why thoughts arise in their hearts, bids them behold his hands and feet and handle him, for a spirit has not flesh and bones as he has, and reminds them that all things must be fulfilled which were written in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms concerning him.

entries.old: Asks the disciples for food and eats fish to confirm his bodily resurrection
entries.new: Jesus asks the disciples whether they have any meat there.

entries.old: Commissions the disciples — repentance and forgiveness will be preached to all nations starting in Jerusalem
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples that thus it is written and thus it behoved Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead the third day, and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations beginning at Jerusalem, declaring them to be witnesses of these things.

entries.old: Peace be with you — as the Father has sent him, so he sends them; receive the Holy Spirit; those whose sins you forgive are forgiven
entries.new: Jesus asks Mary why she weeps and whom she seeks, calls her by name, and tells her not to touch him for he is not yet ascended but to go tell his brethren that he ascends to his Father and their Father, to his God and their God; then appearing to the disciples he says peace be unto you, sends them as the Father has sent him, bids them receive the Holy Ghost, and grants that whose sins they remit are remitted and whose they retain are retained.

entries.old: From the shore he asks the fishermen if they have any meat, and tells them to cast the net on the right side of the ship, where they will find a catch.
entries.new: Jesus calls to the fishermen from the shore asking children if they have any meat, and tells them to cast the net on the right side of the ship and they shall find.

entries.old: He instructs them to bring of the fish which they have just caught.
entries.new: Jesus instructs the disciples to bring of the fish which they have now caught.

entries.old: He invites the disciples, Come and dine.
entries.new: Jesus invites the disciples to come and dine.

entries.old: Returns eight days later with Thomas present and greets the disciples with peace
entries.new: Jesus returns eight days later with Thomas present and greets the disciples, saying peace be unto you.

entries.old: Put your finger here, see his hands, reach into his side — do not disbelieve but believe; blessed are those who have not seen and yet believe
entries.new: Jesus tells Thomas to reach his finger and behold his hands and to reach his hand and thrust it into his side, charging him to be not faithless but believing, and declares that blessed are they who have not seen and yet have believed.

entries.old: Foretells the temple's destruction — not one stone will be left on another
entries.new: Jesus foretells the destruction of the temple, declaring that there shall not be left one stone upon another that shall not be thrown down.

entries.old: Watch out that no one deceives you — many will come claiming to be the Christ; do not be led astray
entries.new: Jesus warns his disciples to take heed that no man deceive them, for many shall come in his name saying I am Christ and shall deceive many; iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold, and many shall be offended and betray and hate one another.

entries.old: Wars, famines, earthquakes, and signs in the heavens — the beginning of birth pains, not yet the end
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples they shall hear of wars and rumours of wars but not be troubled, for nation shall rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there shall be famines, pestilences, and earthquakes in divers places — all these are the beginning of sorrows.

entries.old: The gospel of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the whole world — then the end will come
entries.new: Jesus declares that this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations, and then shall the end come.

entries.old: The abomination of desolation in the holy place — let those in Judea flee; then great tribulation such as has never been
entries.new: Jesus warns that when his hearers see the abomination of desolation spoken of by Daniel standing in the holy place, those in Judaea must flee to the mountains without turning back for their goods, and grieves for those with child and giving suck in those days; for then shall be great tribulation such as has not been since the beginning of the world, and except those days were shortened no flesh should be saved, but for the elect's sake they shall be shortened.

entries.old: Warns that false messiahs and prophets will perform great signs to deceive even the elect
entries.new: Jesus warns that false Christs and false prophets shall arise and shew great signs and wonders, so that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect.

entries.old: The sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light, the stars will fall — the sign of the Son of Man will appear
entries.new: Jesus says that immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun shall be darkened, the moon shall not give her light, the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken; then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven, and all the tribes of the earth shall mourn as they see him coming in the clouds with power and great glory.

entries.old: Foretells the temple's destruction in Mark — every great stone of the buildings will be thrown down
entries.new: Jesus foretells the destruction of the temple, asking his disciples whether they see these great buildings and declaring that there shall not be left one stone upon another that shall not be thrown down.

entries.old: Weeps over Jerusalem — she missed the time of her visitation, and her enemies will leave nothing standing
entries.new: Jesus weeps over Jerusalem, lamenting that if she had known in this her day the things which belong to her peace, but now they are hid from her eyes, for the days shall come when her enemies shall cast a trench about her, compass her round, lay her even with the ground, and not leave one stone upon another, because she knew not the time of her visitation.

entries.old: Foretells the temple's destruction in Luke — the days are coming when not one stone will remain
entries.new: Jesus foretells that the days will come when, of the things they behold, there shall not be left one stone upon another that shall not be thrown down.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Return of the Son of Man
entries.old: Promises that those who endure to the end will be saved
entries.new: Jesus declares that his disciples shall be hated of all men for his name's sake, but he that endures to the end shall be saved.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Return of the Son of Man
entries.old: Promises the Twelve will sit on twelve thrones judging the tribes of Israel when the Son of Man reigns
entries.new: Jesus promises his followers that in the regeneration, when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, they who have followed him shall also sit upon twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Return of the Son of Man
entries.old: As lightning flashes from east to west, so will his coming be — as sudden and unexpected as the days of Noah and Lot
entries.new: Jesus declares that as the lightning comes out of the east and shines even unto the west, so shall the coming of the Son of man be, and that as in the days of Noah they were eating, drinking, marrying, and giving in marriage until the flood came and took them all away, so shall his coming be; he charges them to learn a parable of the fig tree — when its branch is tender and puts forth leaves they know summer is nigh, so when they see all these things they shall know it is near, even at the doors — and declares that heaven and earth shall pass away but his words shall not pass away, and that of that day and hour knows no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but the Father only.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Return of the Son of Man
entries.old: The Son of Man will come on the clouds with power and great glory — his angels will gather the elect from the four winds
entries.new: Jesus declares that the sign of the Son of man shall appear in heaven, and all the tribes of the earth shall mourn as they see him coming in the clouds with power and great glory, and he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet to gather his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Return of the Son of Man
entries.old: One will be taken and one left
entries.new: Jesus says that two shall be in the field, the one taken and the other left, and two women shall be grinding at the mill, the one taken and the other left.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Return of the Son of Man
entries.old: Warns the disciples not to chase rumors of his return — they will long for one of his days but not see it
entries.new: Jesus warns his disciples that the days will come when they shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man and shall not see it, and that when men say see here or see there, they are not to go after them nor follow them.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Return of the Son of Man
entries.old: From the throne declares he makes all things new — promises the water of life to the thirsty and warns the unfaithful of the lake of fire
entries.new: Jesus declares from the throne that he makes all things new, promising the water of life freely to him that is athirst and that he that overcomes shall inherit all things and be his son, while the fearful, unbelieving, abominable, murderers, whoremongers, sorcerers, idolaters, and all liars shall have their part in the lake which burns with fire and brimstone.

entries.old: Watch — you do not know the day or hour; be on guard that hearts are not weighed down with the cares of life
entries.new: Jesus charges his hearers to watch, for they know not what hour their Lord doth come.

entries.old: The faithful and unfaithful servant — who gives food at the proper time versus who abuses his master's absence
entries.new: Jesus tells of a faithful and wise servant whom his lord makes ruler over his household to give them meat in due season and whom his lord, when he comes, shall find so doing and bless by setting him over all his goods; but if that evil servant shall say in his heart that his lord delays his coming and shall begin to smite his fellowservants and eat and drink with the drunken, his lord shall come in a day he looks not for and an hour he is not aware of, and shall cut him asunder and appoint him his portion with the hypocrites where there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

entries.old: The ten virgins — five wise with oil prepared, five foolish who ran out; the door was shut — be ready
entries.new: Jesus likens the kingdom of heaven to ten virgins who took their lamps and went forth to meet the bridegroom — five wise who took oil in their vessels and five foolish who took none — and while the bridegroom tarried they all slumbered and slept; at midnight a cry was made, and the foolish, finding their lamps gone out, went to buy oil, but while they went the bridegroom came and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage and the door was shut, and afterward he answered the others saying he knew them not — therefore watch, for they know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man comes.

entries.old: Calls disciples to be dressed and ready with lamps lit — blessed are the servants their master finds awake
entries.new: Jesus charges his disciples to let their loins be girded about and their lights burning, and to be like men that wait for their lord's return from the wedding to open to him immediately when he knocks; blessed are those servants whom the lord, when he comes, shall find watching, for he shall gird himself and make them sit down to meat and serve them, and they are to be ready also, for the Son of man comes at an hour when they think not.

entries.old: Interrupts the bowl-judgment vision — he comes like a thief; blessed is the one who stays alert and keeps his garments
entries.new: Jesus interrupts the bowl-judgment vision to declare that he comes as a thief, and blessed is he that watches and keeps his garments, lest he walk naked and they see his shame.

entries.old: I am coming soon — blessed is the one who keeps these words; behold, I come quickly
entries.new: Jesus declares behold, I come quickly — blessed is he that keeps the sayings of the prophecy of this book — and that his reward is with him to give every man according as his work shall be, affirming surely I come quickly.

entries.old: I AM the bread of life — whoever comes to me shall not hunger; whoever believes shall not thirst
entries.new: Jesus declares that he is the bread of life and the living bread which came down from heaven, that he who comes to him shall never hunger and he who believes on him shall never thirst, and that the bread he will give for the life of the world is his flesh.

entries.old: I AM the light of the world — whoever follows me will not walk in darkness
entries.new: Jesus declares that he is the light of the world, and that he who follows him shall not walk in darkness but shall have the light of life.

entries.old: Warns that those who do not believe he is who he claims will die in their sins
entries.new: Jesus warns that unless his hearers believe that he is he, they shall die in their sins, and declares that he speaks to the world the things he has heard from the Father who sent him, who is true.

entries.old: Before Abraham was, I AM
entries.new: Jesus declares verily, verily, that before Abraham was, I am.

entries.old: I AM the resurrection and the life — whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live
entries.new: Jesus declares that he is the resurrection and the life, and that he who believes in him, though he were dead, yet shall he live.

entries.old: I AM the way, the truth, and the life — no one comes to the Father except through me
entries.new: Jesus declares that he is the way, the truth, and the life, and that no man comes unto the Father but by him.

entries.old: I AM the true vine, and my Father is the vinedresser
entries.new: Jesus declares that he is the true vine and his Father is the husbandman, and that he is the vine and his disciples are the branches — he that abides in him and he in him brings forth much fruit, for without him they can do nothing.

entries.old: I AM the Alpha and the Omega, the root and offspring of David, the bright morning star
entries.new: Jesus declares that he is Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last, and that he is the root and the offspring of David and the bright and morning star.

entries.old: As a boy in the temple, asks his parents why they searched — he must be about his Father's business
entries.new: Jesus as a boy in the temple asks his parents how it is that they sought him, and whether they did not know that he must be about his Father's business.

entries.old: The Father loves the Son and has given all things into his hand — all things have been delivered to me; no one knows the Son except the Father
entries.new: Jesus declares that the Father loves the Son and has given all things into his hand, that all things are delivered unto him of his Father, and that no man knows the Son but the Father, neither does any know the Father save the Son and he to whom the Son will reveal him.

entries.old: He defends his Sabbath healing by declaring that his Father works until now and he himself works
entries.new: Jesus answers his accusers by declaring that his Father works hitherto, and he works.

entries.old: Teaches that the Son acts only in concert with the Father, who loves the Son and shows him all his works
entries.new: Jesus teaches that the Son can do nothing of himself but what he sees the Father do, and that whatsoever the Father does, these also does the Son likewise, for the Father loves the Son and shows him all things that he himself does, and will show him greater works that they may marvel.

entries.old: Names his witnesses — John the Baptist, his own works, and the Father — to confirm his judgment is just
entries.new: Jesus declares that he can do nothing of himself and that his judgment is just because he seeks not his own will but the will of the Father who sent him, and names as witnesses to him John the Baptist who was a burning and shining light, the works the Father has given him to finish, and the Father himself who has borne witness of him though they have neither heard his voice nor have his word abiding in them.

entries.old: His teaching is not his own but the Father's — anyone willing to do God's will can recognize it as divine
entries.new: Jesus declares that his doctrine is not his own but his that sent him, and that if any man will do God's will he shall know whether the doctrine is of God or whether Jesus speaks of himself, for he that speaks of himself seeks his own glory but he that seeks the glory of him that sent him is true.

entries.old: Tells them they judge by the flesh while he judges no one — yet his judgment is true because the Father is with him
entries.new: Jesus tells his hearers that they judge after the flesh while he judges no man, and that yet if he judges, his judgment is true, for he is not alone but he and the Father that sent him.

entries.old: He tells them they neither know him nor his Father; if they had known him, they would have known the Father also
entries.new: Jesus tells his hearers that they neither know him nor his Father, and that if they had known him they should have known his Father also.

entries.old: His honor comes from the Father — they claim God but do not know him, while the Son knows him and keeps his word
entries.new: Jesus declares that if he honors himself his honor is nothing, but it is his Father that honors him — of whom they say he is their God, yet they have not known him — while he knows him and keeps his saying.

entries.old: I and the Father are one — the Father is in me and I am in the Father
entries.new: Jesus declares that he and his Father are one, and bids his hearers, though they believe not him, to believe the works that they may know and believe that the Father is in him and he in the Father.

entries.old: He asks for which of the many good works shown them from the Father do they seek to stone him
entries.new: Jesus asks for which of the many good works he has shown them from the Father they seek to stone him.

entries.old: Cites Psalm 82 to defend his claim — if Scripture calls others 'gods,' why call it blasphemy when the Son of God claims it?
entries.new: Jesus cites their law that says, ye are gods, and asks why they call it blasphemy when he whom the Father has sanctified and sent into the world says he is the Son of God, since the scripture cannot be broken.

entries.old: To see and believe in the Son is to see and believe in the Father who sent him — he came as light to save, not to judge
entries.new: Jesus declares that he who believes on him believes not on him but on him that sent him, and he who sees him sees him that sent him, and that he is come a light into the world that whoever believes on him should not abide in darkness, for he came not to judge the world but to save it.

entries.old: Affirms his words come from the Father, whose commandment is everlasting life
entries.new: Jesus declares that he has not spoken of himself but the Father who sent him gave him a commandment what he should say and speak, and that he knows the Father's commandment is life everlasting, so whatsoever he speaks he speaks even as the Father said unto him.

entries.old: Tells the disciples that to know him is to know the Father — and from now on they have seen the Father
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples that if they had known him they should have known his Father also, and that from henceforth they know him and have seen him.

entries.old: He who has seen me has seen the Father — I do nothing on my own but speak as the Father taught me
entries.new: Jesus answers Philip, asking how he has been so long with them and yet not known him, and declares that he who has seen him has seen the Father, so why then does Philip say, show us the Father.

entries.old: The Father is greater than I; those who honor the Son honor the Father who sent him
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples that he goes away and comes again unto them, and that if they loved him they would rejoice that he goes to the Father, for his Father is greater than he.

entries.old: Defines his mission — to fulfill the Law, call sinners to repentance, seek the lost, and give his life as ransom
entries.new: Jesus declares that he is not come to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfill them, that he came to call not the righteous but sinners to repentance, that the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost, and to give his life a ransom for many.

entries.old: The Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins and is Lord of the Sabbath
entries.new: Jesus declares that the Son of man has power on earth to forgive sins, and bidding the palsied man arise, take up his bed, and go unto his house, he also names himself Lord even of the sabbath day.

entries.old: A kingdom divided against itself cannot stand
entries.new: Jesus says that every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation and every city or house so divided shall not stand, asks how Satan's kingdom can stand if Satan casts out Satan, declares that if he by the Spirit of God casts out devils then the kingdom of God is come unto them, likens his work to one binding the strong man before spoiling his house, and warns that he that is not with him is against him and he that gathers not with him scatters abroad.

entries.old: Counters the chief priests' challenge with a question — the baptism of John, whence was it, from heaven or of men?
entries.new: Jesus answers the chief priests' challenge by saying he will tell them by what authority he acts if they first answer him whether the baptism of John was from heaven or of men.

entries.old: Refuses to answer when they would not commit — neither tell I you by what authority I do these things
entries.new: Jesus tells the chief priests that neither will he tell them by what authority he does these things.

entries.old: All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me
entries.new: Jesus declares that all power is given unto him in heaven and in earth.

entries.old: Reminds the Pharisees that hungry David ate the showbread reserved for priests
entries.new: Jesus asks the Pharisees whether they have never read what David did when he was hungered, how he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest and ate the shewbread which was not lawful for any but the priests, and gave also to those with him.

entries.old: Calls a man with a withered hand forward and asks whether it is lawful to do good or save life on the Sabbath
entries.new: Jesus bids the man with the withered hand to stand forth, asks whether it is lawful to do good on the sabbath days or to do evil, to save life or to kill, and then commands him to stretch forth his hand.

entries.old: He came to cast fire on the earth — not peace but a sword
entries.new: Jesus says that he is come to send fire on the earth, and asks what he will if it be already kindled.

entries.old: He tells his mother at Cana that his hour has not yet come
entries.new: Jesus says to his mother at Cana, Woman, what have I to do with thee, and tells her that his hour is not yet come.

entries.old: He tells the disciples he has meat to eat that they know nothing of
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples that he has meat to eat that they know not of.

entries.old: Tells the disciples the man's blindness is not from sin but exists so God's works can be revealed in him
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples that neither this man nor his parents have sinned, but that the works of God should be made manifest in him, and says that he must work the works of him that sent him while it is day, for the night comes when no man can work.

entries.old: Tells the disciples Lazarus's sickness will not end in death but will glorify God and the Son of God
entries.new: Jesus says that this sickness is not unto death but for the glory of God, that the Son of God might be glorified thereby.

entries.old: Tells the disciples Lazarus has fallen asleep and he is going to wake him — those who walk by day do not stumble
entries.new: Jesus asks whether there are not twelve hours in the day, says that he who walks in the day stumbles not because he sees the light of this world while he who walks in the night stumbles for there is no light in him, and tells the disciples that their friend Lazarus sleeps and he goes to awake him out of sleep.

entries.old: He assures Martha that her brother shall rise again.
entries.new: Jesus assures Martha that her brother shall rise again.

entries.old: He descended from heaven and is from above — not of this world; before Abraham was, I AM
entries.new: Jesus declares that no man has ascended up to heaven but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven.

entries.old: Came from heaven to do the Father's will — to lose none given to him but raise them up at the last day
entries.new: Jesus says that he is come down from heaven not to do his own will but the will of him that sent him, and that the Father's will is that of all the Father has given him he should lose nothing but should raise it up again at the last day.

entries.old: He tells the crowd not to murmur among themselves
entries.new: Jesus tells the crowd to murmur not among themselves.

entries.old: He asks the murmuring disciples whether his teaching offends them, and what if they should see the Son of Man ascend up where he was before
entries.new: Jesus asks the murmuring disciples whether his saying offends them, and what if they shall see the Son of man ascend up where he was before.

entries.old: Tells his brothers his time has not come — the world hates him because he testifies its works are evil
entries.new: Jesus tells his brothers that his time is not yet come while their time is always ready, that the world cannot hate them but it hates him because he testifies of it that its works are evil, and bids them go up to the feast though he goes not up yet, for his time is not yet full come.

entries.old: He cries in the temple that he is not come of himself but is from him who sent him; he knows the Father, but they do not
entries.new: Jesus cries in the temple that though they know him and know whence he is, he is not come of himself but is sent by one who is true, whom they know not, and that he knows him for he is from him and sent by him.

entries.old: Foretells he will soon return to the Father — and they cannot follow where he goes
entries.new: Jesus says that yet a little while is he with them, and then he goes unto him that sent him, and that they shall seek him and not find him, for where he is they cannot come.

entries.old: He came from the Father into the world and now returns to the Father
entries.new: Jesus says that he came forth from the Father and is come into the world, and now leaves the world and goes to the Father.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
entries.old: As Jonah was in the fish three days, so will the Son of Man be in the earth; destroy this temple and in three days I will raise it
entries.new: Jesus declares that as Jonah was three days and three nights in the whale's belly, so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
entries.old: The Son of Man must suffer many things, be rejected, be killed, and rise on the third day
entries.new: Jesus foretells that the Son of man must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, be killed, and be raised again the third day.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
entries.old: Rebukes Peter for opposing the cross — 'Get behind me, Satan' — Peter's mind is on man's things, not God's
entries.new: Jesus rebukes Peter, saying get thee behind me Satan, for he is an offence and savours not the things of God but the things that be of men.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
entries.old: Charges Peter, James, and John to keep the Transfiguration secret until after his resurrection
entries.new: Jesus charges Peter, James, and John to tell the vision to no man until the Son of man is risen again from the dead.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
entries.old: Affirms Elijah has already come and was mistreated — and the Son of Man will suffer the same way
entries.new: Jesus affirms that Elijah truly comes first and restores all things, but says that Elijah has already come and they knew him not and have done to him whatever they wished, and that likewise the Son of man shall suffer of them.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
entries.old: Rebukes Peter for opposing his foretold suffering — 'Get behind me, Satan'
entries.new: Jesus rebukes Peter, saying get thee behind me Satan, for he savours not the things that be of God but the things that be of men.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
entries.old: Speaks of the baptism of suffering ahead and how distressed he is until it is accomplished
entries.new: Jesus says that he has a baptism to be baptized with, and how straitened he is till it be accomplished.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
entries.old: Everything written about him in the Prophets will be accomplished; the Christ must suffer and rise on the third day
entries.new: Jesus tells the twelve that they go up to Jerusalem and all things written by the prophets concerning the Son of man shall be accomplished, for he shall be delivered to the Gentiles and mocked and spitefully entreated and spat upon, and they shall scourge him and put him to death, and the third day he shall rise again.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
entries.old: Foretells he will be handed to the Gentiles, mocked, scourged, killed — and rise on the third day
entries.new: Jesus foretells that he shall be delivered to the Gentiles, mocked, spitefully entreated, spat upon, scourged, and put to death, and that the third day he shall rise again.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
entries.old: He drives out the dove sellers from the temple, declaring that his Father's house must not be made a house of merchandise
entries.new: Jesus drives the dove sellers from the temple, charging them to take these things away and not to make his Father's house a house of merchandise.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
entries.old: As Moses lifted up the serpent, so must the Son of Man be lifted up — and when lifted, will draw all people
entries.new: Jesus declares that as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up, that whosoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
entries.old: The good shepherd lays down his life of his own accord; unless a grain of wheat falls and dies, it cannot bear fruit
entries.new: Jesus declares that the Father loves him because he lays down his life that he might take it again, that no man takes it from him but he lays it down of himself, and that he has power to lay it down and power to take it again, this commandment having been received from his Father.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
entries.old: He defends Mary's anointing — she has kept this for the day of his burying; the poor are always with you, but he will not always be present.
entries.new: Jesus defends Mary's anointing, saying to let her alone for she has kept this against the day of his burying, and that the poor they have always with them but him they have not always.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
entries.old: Announces that the hour for the Son of Man to be glorified has come
entries.new: Jesus announces that the hour is come that the Son of man should be glorified.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
entries.old: Warns them in advance so they will believe — the prince of this world comes but has no claim on him
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples beforehand so that when it comes to pass they may believe, and says that the prince of this world is coming and has nothing in him, but that the world may know he loves the Father he does as the Father has commanded — arise, let us go hence.

entries.old: Submits to John's baptism — it is fitting to fulfill all righteousness
entries.new: Jesus tells John to suffer it to be so now, for thus it becomes them to fulfill all righteousness.

entries.old: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the dead are raised, the poor have good news — blessed is he who does not stumble over me
entries.new: Jesus tells John's disciples to report what they hear and see — the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have the gospel preached to them — and blessed is whosoever shall not be offended in him.

entries.old: Identifies John the Baptist as the prophesied Elijah for those willing to accept it
entries.new: Jesus says that if his hearers will receive it, John is the Elijah who was to come.

entries.old: Defends his disciples by citing David eating the showbread and priests working on the Sabbath — one greater than the temple is here
entries.new: Jesus defends his disciples by recalling how David and his men ate the showbread that was not lawful for them, and how the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and are blameless, declaring that in this place is one greater than the temple.

entries.old: Defines his earthly mission — sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel
entries.new: Jesus declares that he is not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

entries.old: Asks the disciples at Caesarea Philippi — whom do men say that I the Son of man am?
entries.new: Jesus asks his disciples at Caesarea Philippi whom men say that he, the Son of man, is.

entries.old: Presses the disciples to confess for themselves who they say he is
entries.new: Jesus presses the disciples, asking whom they themselves say that he is.

entries.old: Blesses Peter for his confession — flesh and blood did not reveal it to him, but the Father in heaven
entries.new: Jesus blesses Simon Bar-jona, declaring that flesh and blood has not revealed it to him but the Father in heaven.

entries.old: Reassures the disciples after the Transfiguration — arise, and be not afraid
entries.new: Jesus reassures the disciples after the Transfiguration, telling them to arise and be not afraid.

entries.old: Teaches Peter that the sons are free from the temple tax, but provides it from a coin in a fish's mouth to avoid offense
entries.new: Jesus teaches Peter that the kings of the earth take tribute from strangers and not from their own children, so the children are free, but lest they offend, he sends Peter to cast a hook into the sea, take the first fish that comes up, and find in its mouth a piece of money to give for the two of them.

entries.old: Declares his mission to seek the lost — for the Son of man is come to save that which was lost
entries.new: Jesus declares that the Son of man is come to save that which was lost.

entries.old: Sends two disciples to fetch the colt for the triumphal entry — tell the owner the Lord has need of it
entries.new: Jesus sends two disciples into the village to find an ass tied with a colt, to loose them and bring them, and if any man says ought to them they shall say the Lord has need of them, and straightway he will send them.

entries.old: Silences the Pharisees with a question about Christ — whose son is he? If David in spirit calls him Lord, how is he his son?
entries.new: Jesus asks the Pharisees what they think of Christ and whose son he is, then citing David who in spirit calls him Lord — saying the LORD said unto my Lord, sit thou on my right hand till I make thine enemies thy footstool — he asks how, if David then calls him Lord, he is his son.

entries.old: Affirms that Elijah comes first to restore all things — and has already come and been mistreated
entries.new: Jesus affirms that Elijah verily comes first and restores all things, and that as it is written of the Son of man he must suffer many things and be set at nought, but says that Elijah is indeed already come and they have done to him whatever they wished, as it is written of him.

entries.old: Reads Isaiah 61 in the Nazareth synagogue and declares the scripture fulfilled — the Spirit of the Lord has anointed him; today this is fulfilled in your ears
entries.new: Jesus reads from Isaiah in the Nazareth synagogue and declares to the hearers that this day is this scripture fulfilled in their ears.

entries.old: Defends the disciples' praise at the triumphal entry — if they were silent, even the stones would cry out
entries.new: Jesus tells the Pharisees that if his disciples should hold their peace, the stones would immediately cry out.

entries.old: He greets Nathanael as a true Israelite without guile and reveals he saw him under the fig tree before Philip called
entries.new: Jesus greets Nathanael as an Israelite indeed in whom is no guile, and tells him that before Philip called him, when he was under the fig tree, he saw him.

entries.old: Promises Nathanael will see greater things — heaven open and angels ascending and descending on the Son of Man
