entries.new: Jesus promises Nathanael that he shall see greater things than these, and that hereafter he shall see heaven open and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man.

entries.old: He asks the Samaritan woman at the well to give him a drink
entries.new: Jesus asks the Samaritan woman at the well to give him to drink.

entries.old: He tells the woman to call her husband and reveals he knows she has had five husbands and the man she now has is not her husband
entries.new: Jesus tells the Samaritan woman to go call her husband, then says she has well said she has no husband, for she has had five husbands and the man she now has is not her husband.

entries.old: He declares to the Samaritan woman: I who speak to you am the Messiah
entries.new: Jesus declares to the Samaritan woman that he who speaks to her is he, the Messiah.

entries.old: He reveals himself to the healed man, declaring that the one who talks with him is the Son of God
entries.new: Jesus reveals himself to the healed man, telling him that he has both seen him and that it is he who talks with him.

entries.old: The works done in the Father's name bear witness — if not doing the Father's works, do not believe
entries.new: Jesus says that the works he does in his Father's name bear witness of him, charging his hearers that if he does not the works of his Father they should not believe him, but if he does, though they believe not him let them believe the works, that they may know and believe that the Father is in him and he in the Father.

entries.old: Announces the Son of Man is now glorified and warns the disciples he will be with them only a little while longer
entries.new: Jesus announces that now is the Son of man glorified and God is glorified in him, and warns his little children that yet a little while he is with them, that they shall seek him, and as he said to the Jews, whither he goes they cannot come.

entries.old: Cleanses a leper with a touch and instructs him to show himself to the priest and offer the gift Moses commanded as a testimony
entries.new: Jesus tells the kneeling leper that he is willing and commands him to be clean, then charges him to tell no one but to show himself to the priest and offer the gift Moses commanded as a testimony unto them.

entries.old: Responds to the centurion's request for his servant — I will come and heal him
entries.new: Jesus answers the centurion's plea for his stricken servant by declaring that he will come and heal him.

entries.old: Authorizes demons to enter the herd of swine with a single word — Go
entries.new: Jesus answers the legion of demons begging to enter the swine with a single word, and bids them go.

entries.old: Charges the healed blind men to silence — see that no man know it
entries.new: Jesus, having opened the eyes of the two blind men, straitly charges them to see that no man know of it.

entries.old: Heals a man's withered hand on the Sabbath
entries.new: Jesus calls the man with the withered hand to stretch it forth, and it is restored whole as the other on the Sabbath.

entries.old: Calls for the loaves and fishes before feeding the five thousand — bring them hither to me
entries.new: Jesus calls for the five loaves and two fishes to be brought to him before he feeds the five thousand.

entries.old: Asks the disciples how many loaves they have before feeding the four thousand
entries.new: Jesus asks the disciples how many loaves they have before he feeds the four thousand.

entries.old: Rebukes an unclean spirit in the Capernaum synagogue, commanding it to be silent and come out
entries.new: Jesus rebukes the unclean spirit in the Capernaum synagogue, charging it to hold its peace and come out of the man.

entries.old: Peace, be still — Jesus rebukes the wind and commands the sea, and there was a great calm
entries.new: Jesus rebukes the wind and commands the raging sea to be at peace and be still, and there is a great calm.

entries.old: Confronts the Gerasene demoniac, asking the unclean spirit its name — Legion
entries.new: Jesus charges the unclean spirit to come out of the Gerasene man and demands its name, which answers Legion, for they are many.

entries.old: Perceives that virtue has gone out of him and asks who touched him in the crowd
entries.new: Jesus, perceiving that virtue has gone out of him, turns in the press of the crowd and asks who touched his clothes.

entries.old: Silences the mourners at Jairus's house declaring the girl is not dead but sleeping, then raises her with the words 'Talitha cumi'
entries.new: Jesus silences the weeping mourners at Jairus's house, declaring that the damsel is not dead but sleepeth, then takes her by the hand and raises her with the words Talitha cumi.

entries.old: Tells the disciples to feed the crowd themselves and asks how many loaves they have — sets up the feeding of five thousand
entries.new: Jesus charges the disciples to give the crowd to eat themselves and bids them go and see how many loaves they have, before the feeding of the five thousand.

entries.old: Ephphatha — Be opened — Jesus heals the deaf man with an impeded speech impediment
entries.new: Jesus looks up to heaven, sighs, and says Ephphatha, that is, Be opened, and the deaf man's ears and tongue are loosed.

entries.old: Has compassion on the crowd that has gone three days without food and resolves to feed them before sending them home
entries.new: Jesus declares his compassion on the multitude that has been with him three days with nothing to eat, and will not send them away fasting lest they faint by the way, for some have come from far.

entries.old: Casts out a deaf and mute spirit from a boy and forbids it to return
entries.new: Jesus charges the dumb and deaf spirit to come out of the boy and to enter no more into him.

entries.old: Asks blind Bartimaeus what he wants and restores his sight, declaring his faith has made him whole
entries.new: Jesus asks blind Bartimaeus what he would have done unto him, and upon his plea to receive his sight bids him go his way, declaring that his faith has made him whole.

entries.old: Raises the widow's son at Nain from his bier with a word
entries.new: Jesus tells the weeping widow of Nain not to weep, then touches the bier and calls her dead son to arise.

entries.old: Turns water into wine at Cana — instructs the servants to fill the jars and serve the master of the feast
entries.new: Jesus instructs the servants at Cana to fill the waterpots with water, then to draw out and bear it unto the governor of the feast, turning the water into wine.

entries.old: He sends the nobleman home with the word that his son lives, healing the boy at a distance
entries.new: Jesus sends the nobleman on his way with the word that his son lives, healing the boy at a distance.

entries.old: He commands the lame man to rise, take up his bed, and walk
entries.new: Jesus asks the man infirm thirty-eight years at Bethesda whether he will be made whole, then commands him to rise, take up his bed, and walk.

entries.old: He asks Philip where they shall buy bread to feed the great multitude that has come to him
entries.new: Jesus asks Philip whence they shall buy bread that the great multitude coming to him may eat.

entries.old: He instructs the disciples to make the men sit down before the feeding of the five thousand
entries.new: Jesus instructs the disciples to make the men sit down before the feeding of the five thousand.

entries.old: He tells the disciples to gather up the leftover fragments so that nothing be lost
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples to gather up the fragments that remain so that nothing be lost.

entries.old: He sends the man born blind to wash in the pool of Siloam, and the man returns seeing
entries.new: Jesus sends the man born blind to go and wash in the pool of Siloam, and the man returns seeing.

entries.old: At Lazarus's tomb, commands the stone removed, thanks the Father, and calls Lazarus out
entries.new: At Lazarus's tomb Jesus commands the stone be taken away, reminds Martha that if she would believe she should see the glory of God, lifts his eyes to thank the Father for hearing him so that the people standing by may believe the Father has sent him, then cries with a loud voice for Lazarus to come forth and bids them loose him and let him go.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Promise and Coming of the Spirit
entries.old: Promises the Father will send another Helper, the Spirit of truth, to dwell with them forever
entries.new: Jesus says he will pray the Father, who shall give them another Comforter, even the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive because it neither sees nor knows him, but who dwells with them and shall be in them forever.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Promise and Coming of the Spirit
entries.old: Promises not to leave them as orphans — he will come to them, and those who keep his commandments will be loved by the Father
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples he will not leave them comfortless but will come to them, that because he lives they shall live also, and that the one who has his commandments and keeps them is the one who loves him and shall be loved of his Father, to whom he will manifest himself.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Promise and Coming of the Spirit
entries.old: The Helper, sent in his name, will teach all things, bring his words to remembrance, and bear witness about him
entries.new: Jesus says the Comforter, the Holy Ghost whom the Father will send in his name, shall teach them all things and bring to their remembrance whatever he has said to them.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Promise and Coming of the Spirit
entries.old: Tells them his departure is for their good — only then will the Helper come and guide them into all truth
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples it is expedient for them that he go away, for if he does not depart the Comforter will not come, but when the Spirit of truth is come he will guide them into all truth, speaking what he hears and showing them things to come, and shall glorify Jesus by receiving what is his and showing it to them.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Promise and Coming of the Spirit
entries.old: Wait for the promise of the Father — baptized with the Holy Spirit; you will receive power and be his witnesses; receive the Holy Spirit
entries.new: Jesus charges his disciples to wait for the promise of the Father, declaring that John baptized with water but they shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost not many days hence, and that they shall receive power after the Holy Ghost is come upon them and shall be his witnesses in Jerusalem, in all Judaea and Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Promise and Coming of the Spirit
entries.old: Peter recalls the word of the Lord: John baptized with water, but you shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit
entries.new: Jesus says that John indeed baptized with water but they shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Spirit's Work in the World
entries.old: Assures the disciples the Father gives the Holy Spirit to those who ask
entries.new: Jesus says that if those who are evil know how to give good gifts to their children, how much more shall the heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Spirit's Work in the World
entries.old: The Spirit gives life; the flesh profits nothing; out of the believer will flow rivers of living water
entries.new: Jesus declares that it is the Spirit that quickens and the flesh profits nothing, and that the words he speaks are spirit and are life.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Spirit's Work in the World
entries.old: The Spirit will convict the world of sin (unbelief), righteousness (Jesus's return to the Father), and judgment (the ruler of this world condemned)
entries.new: Jesus says that when the Comforter is come he will reprove the world of sin because they believe not on him, of righteousness because he goes to the Father and they see him no more, and of judgment because the prince of this world is judged.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Spirit's Work in the World
entries.old: Tells the disciples there is more to say, but they cannot bear it yet
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples he has yet many things to say to them, but they cannot bear them now.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Spirit's Work in the World
entries.old: Tells them all the Father has is his, so the Spirit will reveal it — and soon they will see him again
entries.new: Jesus declares that all things the Father has are his, and therefore the Spirit shall take of his and show it to them, and that in a little while they shall not see him and again a little while and they shall see him because he goes to the Father.

entries.old: Every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven, but blasphemy against the Spirit will not — in this age or the age to come
entries.new: Jesus says that all manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven men, but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven, and whoever speaks a word against the Son of man shall be forgiven, but whoever speaks against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven, neither in this world nor in the world to come.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Certainty and Scope of Judgment
entries.old: It will be more tolerable for Sodom than for those who reject his messengers; all in the tombs will come out — the good to life, the evil to judgment
entries.new: Jesus declares that it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment than for the city that rejects his messengers, and says that the hour comes when all who are in the graves shall hear his voice and come forth — they that have done good to the resurrection of life, and they that have done evil to the resurrection of damnation.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Certainty and Scope of Judgment
entries.old: People will give account for every careless word; the word he has spoken will judge those who reject him on the last day
entries.new: Jesus says that every idle word men speak they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment, and declares that the word he has spoken shall judge those who reject him at the last day.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Certainty and Scope of Judgment
entries.old: Nineveh and the Queen of the South will rise in judgment against this generation — for a greater than Jonas and Solomon is here
entries.new: Jesus declares that the men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation and condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonas, and that the queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation and condemn it, for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon — and a greater than Jonas and a greater than Solomon is here.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Certainty and Scope of Judgment
entries.old: The Son of Man will come in glory with his angels and repay each according to his works; the Father has given all judgment to the Son
entries.new: Jesus says that the Son of man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels and shall reward every man according to his works, for the Father has committed all judgment unto the Son.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Certainty and Scope of Judgment
entries.old: He says he goes his way and they shall seek him and die in their sins, for where he goes they cannot come
entries.new: Jesus says that he goes his way and his hearers shall seek him and shall die in their sins, for whither he goes they cannot come.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Certainty and Scope of Judgment
entries.old: Tells the crowd the voice from heaven came for them — judgment falls on this world and its ruler is driven out
entries.new: Jesus tells the crowd that the voice from heaven came not because of him but for their sakes, and declares that now is the judgment of this world and now shall the prince of this world be cast out.

entries.old: Whoever calls his brother a fool is in danger of the fire of Gehenna — anger begins the progression toward judgment
entries.new: Jesus warns that whoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment, that whoever shall say to his brother Raca shall be in danger of the council, and that whoever shall say Thou fool shall be in danger of hell fire.

entries.old: If your right eye causes you to sin, tear it out — better to lose a member than have your whole body cast into Gehenna
entries.new: Jesus charges that if the right eye offend a man let him pluck it out and cast it from him, and if the right hand offend let him cut it off and cast it from him, for it is profitable that one of his members should perish rather than his whole body be cast into hell.

entries.old: The sons of the kingdom shall be cast into outer darkness — there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth
entries.new: Jesus declares that the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness, where there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

entries.old: Fear him who has authority to destroy both soul and body in hell — do not fear those who can only kill the body
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples to fear not them which kill the body but are not able to kill the soul, but rather to fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.

entries.old: At the end of the age the angels will cast the wicked into the furnace of fire — there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth
entries.new: Jesus declares that at the end of the age the angels shall cast the wicked into a furnace of fire, where there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth.

entries.old: Better to enter life maimed than be cast into Gehenna with unquenchable fire — where the worm does not die and the fire is not quenched
entries.new: Jesus says that if a hand or foot offend a man, let him cut it off and cast it from him, for it is better to enter into life halt or maimed than having two hands or two feet to be cast into everlasting fire — into hell, where their worm dies not and the fire is not quenched.

entries.old: Bind him and cast him into outer darkness — parabolic warnings of outer darkness at the judgment
entries.new: Jesus tells how the king commands his servants to bind the man hand and foot and cast him into outer darkness, where there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

entries.old: How shall you escape the damnation of hell — serpents, brood of vipers
entries.new: Jesus cries out to the scribes and Pharisees, calling them serpents and a generation of vipers, and asks how they shall escape the damnation of hell.

entries.old: Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil — eternal punishment versus eternal life
entries.new: Jesus declares that he will say to those on his left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels, and that these shall go away into everlasting punishment but the righteous into life eternal.

entries.old: Foretells that Gentiles will come from every direction to feast in the kingdom with the patriarchs
entries.new: Jesus declares that many shall come from the east and west and shall sit down with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.

entries.old: The dead will hear the voice of the Son of God and live — I am the resurrection and the life; I will raise him up on the last day
entries.new: Jesus declares that the hour is coming and now is when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God and they that hear shall live, says that he is the resurrection and the life and that he that believes in him though he were dead yet shall live, and promises to raise up at the last day every one the Father has given him.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Introduction to the Seven Churches — The Vision of Christ
entries.old: Declares himself the Alpha and Omega, the Almighty Lord God who is and was and is to come
entries.new: Jesus declares that he is Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, the Lord who is and was and is to come, the Almighty.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Introduction to the Seven Churches — The Vision of Christ
entries.old: The risen Jesus commands John to write in a book what he sees and send it to the seven churches: Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea.
entries.new: Jesus, the first and the last, charges John to write what he sees in a book and send it to the seven churches in Asia — Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamos, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Introduction to the Seven Churches — The Vision of Christ
entries.old: I AM the First and the Last, the Living One — dead, and behold alive forevermore; I hold the keys of death and Hades
entries.new: Jesus tells John not to fear, declaring that he is the first and the last, the living one who was dead and is alive for evermore, and holds the keys of hell and of death.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Introduction to the Seven Churches — The Vision of Christ
entries.old: Tells John to write what he has seen, what is, and what is to come — and reveals the meaning of the stars and lampstands
entries.new: Jesus charges John to write the things he has seen, the things which are, and the things which shall be hereafter, and reveals that the seven stars in his right hand are the angels of the seven churches and the seven golden candlesticks are the churches themselves.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Introduction to the Seven Churches — The Vision of Christ
entries.old: Closes each of the seven letters with the same summons to spiritual attention — he who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches
entries.new: Jesus closes each of the seven letters with the same summons, charging him that has an ear to hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Ephesus — The Church That Left Its First Love
entries.old: Addresses Ephesus as the one who holds the seven stars and walks among the seven golden lampstands
entries.new: Jesus addresses the angel of the church of Ephesus as the one who holds the seven stars in his right hand and walks in the midst of the seven golden candlesticks.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Ephesus — The Church That Left Its First Love
entries.old: Commends their toil, endurance, and testing of false apostles — but they have abandoned their first love; remember, repent, and return to those works
entries.new: Jesus commends Ephesus for their works, labor, patience, and testing of false apostles, but holds against them that they have left their first love, charging them to remember from where they have fallen, repent, and do the first works, or else he will come quickly and remove their candlestick out of its place.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Ephesus — The Church That Left Its First Love
entries.old: Yet this you have to your credit: you hate the deeds of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate
entries.new: Jesus commends Ephesus that they hate the deeds of the Nicolaitans, which he also hates.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Ephesus — The Church That Left Its First Love
entries.old: To the one who conquers: I will grant to eat of the tree of life in the paradise of God
entries.new: Jesus promises that to him who overcomes he will give to eat of the tree of life which is in the midst of the paradise of God.

entries.old: Addresses Smyrna as the First and the Last, who was dead and is alive
entries.new: Jesus addresses the angel of the church in Smyrna as the first and the last, who was dead and is alive.

entries.old: Tells suffering Smyrna they are spiritually rich — do not fear, be faithful even to death
entries.new: Jesus tells Smyrna that he knows their tribulation and poverty, though they are rich, and the blasphemy of those who say they are Jews and are not but are the synagogue of Satan, charging them not to fear what they shall suffer but to be faithful unto death, and he will give them a crown of life.

entries.old: To the one who conquers: the crown of life; will not be hurt by the second death
entries.new: Jesus charges Smyrna to be faithful unto death for the crown of life, and promises that he who overcomes shall not be hurt of the second death.

entries.old: Addresses Pergamum as the one who wields the sharp two-edged sword
entries.new: Jesus addresses the angel of the church in Pergamos as the one who has the sharp sword with two edges.

entries.old: You have held fast my name and not denied my faith — but some hold the teaching of Balaam and practice sexual immorality; repent or I will war against them
entries.new: Jesus commends Pergamos for holding fast his name and not denying his faith even where Satan dwells and where Antipas his faithful martyr was slain, but holds against them that some there hold the doctrine of Balaam and of the Nicolaitans, charging them to repent or he will come quickly and fight against them with the sword of his mouth.

entries.old: To the one who conquers: hidden manna and a white stone with a new name
entries.new: Jesus promises that to him who overcomes he will give to eat of the hidden manna and a white stone with a new name written on it which no man knows save he who receives it.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Thyatira — The Church Tolerating False Teaching
entries.old: Addresses Thyatira as the Son of God with eyes of fire and feet of burnished bronze
entries.new: Jesus addresses the angel of the church in Thyatira as the Son of God, whose eyes are like a flame of fire and whose feet are like fine brass.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Thyatira — The Church Tolerating False Teaching
entries.old: Commends Thyatira's love and service but rebukes their tolerance of Jezebel — he searches hearts and judges by works
entries.new: Jesus commends Thyatira's works, charity, service, faith, and patience, but holds against them that they suffer the woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess and seduces his servants to fornication and to eat things sacrificed to idols, and declares that he will cast her into a bed and her children he will kill with death, that all the churches may know he is he who searches the reins and hearts and gives to every one according to their works.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Thyatira — The Church Tolerating False Teaching
entries.old: Tells the faithful remnant at Thyatira he places no further burden on them — only hold what they have until he comes
entries.new: Jesus tells the rest in Thyatira who have not held this doctrine nor known the depths of Satan that he will put on them no other burden.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Thyatira — The Church Tolerating False Teaching
entries.old: Hold fast what you have until I come; to the one who conquers: authority over the nations and the morning star
entries.new: Jesus charges Thyatira to hold fast what they have until he comes, and promises that to him who overcomes and keeps his works to the end he will give power over the nations to rule them with a rod of iron, and will give him the morning star.

entries.old: You have a reputation of being alive but are dead — wake up and strengthen what remains; remember, keep it, and repent; if not, I will come like a thief
entries.new: Jesus, who has the seven Spirits of God and the seven stars, tells Sardis that they have a name that they live but are dead, charging them to be watchful and strengthen the things which remain, to remember how they have received and heard, to hold fast and repent, or else he will come on them as a thief at an hour they do not know.

entries.old: Honors the few in Sardis who kept their garments clean — they will walk with him in white
entries.new: Jesus says that there are a few names in Sardis who have not defiled their garments, and they shall walk with him in white, for they are worthy.

entries.old: To the one who conquers: clothed in white; name not blotted from the book of life; acknowledged before the Father
entries.new: Jesus promises that he who overcomes shall be clothed in white raiment, and that he will not blot his name out of the book of life but will confess his name before the Father and before his angels.

entries.old: Addresses Philadelphia as the holy and true one who holds the key of David, opening and shutting at will
entries.new: Jesus addresses the angel of the church in Philadelphia as he that is holy, he that is true, who has the key of David, who opens and no man shuts, and shuts and no man opens.

entries.old: I have set before you an open door no one can shut; you have kept my word and not denied my name; I will keep you from the hour of trial
entries.new: Jesus tells Philadelphia that he has set before them an open door no man can shut, for they have a little strength and have kept his word and not denied his name, and declares that he will make those of the synagogue of Satan come and worship before their feet, and because they have kept the word of his patience he will keep them from the hour of temptation that shall come upon all the world.

entries.old: I am coming soon — hold fast so no one seizes your crown; to the one who conquers: a pillar in God's temple with the name of God and the new Jerusalem
entries.new: Jesus says he comes quickly and charges Philadelphia to hold fast what they have so that no man takes their crown, and promises that him who overcomes he will make a pillar in the temple of his God, and will write on him the name of his God and the name of the city of his God, the new Jerusalem, and his own new name.

entries.old: Addresses Laodicea as the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of God's creation
entries.new: Jesus addresses the angel of the church of the Laodiceans as the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God.

entries.old: Rebukes lukewarm Laodicea — they boast wealth but are poor, blind, and naked; he rebukes those he loves
entries.new: Jesus rebukes Laodicea for being neither cold nor hot but lukewarm, declaring that he will spue them out of his mouth, and tells them that though they say they are rich and have need of nothing, they know not that they are wretched, miserable, poor, blind, and naked, counseling them to buy of him gold tried in the fire, white raiment, and eyesalve, and declaring that as many as he loves he rebukes and chastens, charging them therefore to be zealous and repent.

entries.old: Behold, I stand at the door and knock — if anyone opens I will come in; to the one who conquers: I will grant to sit with me on my throne
entries.new: Jesus says that he stands at the door and knocks, and that if any man hears his voice and opens the door he will come in and sup with him, and promises that to him who overcomes he will grant to sit with him on his throne, even as he also overcame and is set down with the Father on his throne.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Nature and Character of the Kingdom
entries.old: Many from east and west will come and recline at table in the kingdom
entries.new: Jesus declares that many shall come from the east and west and sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven, while the children of the kingdom shall be cast into outer darkness where there is weeping and gnashing of teeth.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Nature and Character of the Kingdom
entries.old: The kingdom has been forcefully advancing since the days of John; it has been given to those who will produce its fruit
entries.new: Jesus says that from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffers violence and the violent take it by force, and warns that the kingdom of God shall be taken from those who do not bring forth its fruit and given to a nation that will.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Nature and Character of the Kingdom
entries.old: Kingdom of heaven compared to leaven hidden in three measures of flour — permeates the whole
entries.new: Jesus likens the kingdom of heaven to leaven which a woman takes and hides in three measures of meal until the whole is leavened.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Nature and Character of the Kingdom
entries.old: Kingdom compared to treasure hidden in a field, and to a merchant who sells everything for one pearl of great value — worth giving up everything
entries.new: Jesus likens the kingdom of heaven to treasure hid in a field which a man, having found, hides and for joy sells all that he has to buy that field, and again to a merchant seeking goodly pearls who, finding one of great price, sells all that he has and buys it.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Nature and Character of the Kingdom
entries.old: Kingdom compared to a net cast into the sea — gathers all kinds, sorted at the end of the age
entries.new: Jesus likens the kingdom of heaven to a net cast into the sea that gathers of every kind, which when full is drawn to shore so that the good are gathered into vessels and the bad cast away, and declares that so shall it be at the end of the world when the angels sever the wicked from among the just and cast them into the furnace of fire where there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Nature and Character of the Kingdom
entries.old: Likens the trained kingdom scribe to a householder who brings out treasures both new and old
entries.new: Jesus likens every scribe instructed unto the kingdom of heaven to a householder who brings forth out of his treasure things both new and old.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Nature and Character of the Kingdom
entries.old: Kingdom compared to a king who gave a wedding banquet — those invited refused, so the invitation went out to all
entries.new: Jesus likens the kingdom of heaven to a king who makes a marriage for his son and sends his servants to call those who were bidden, but they refuse and even kill the servants, so the king destroys them, burns their city, and sends his servants into the highways to gather all they find, both bad and good; when one is found at the feast without a wedding garment he is bound and cast into outer darkness, for many are called but few are chosen.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Nature and Character of the Kingdom
entries.old: Kingdom of heaven compared to ten virgins awaiting the bridegroom — be ready
entries.new: Jesus likens the kingdom of heaven to ten virgins who take their lamps and go forth to meet the bridegroom — five wise who take oil in their vessels and five foolish who take none — and while the bridegroom tarries they all sleep, but at midnight a cry is made and the wise enter in with him to the marriage while the foolish, gone to buy oil, return to a shut door and hear, I know you not, so he charges his hearers to watch, for they know neither the day nor the hour.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Nature and Character of the Kingdom
entries.old: Begins his Galilean ministry by proclaiming the kingdom of God is at hand and calling for repentance
entries.new: Jesus proclaims that the time is fulfilled and the kingdom of God is at hand, and calls his hearers to repent and believe the gospel.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Nature and Character of the Kingdom
entries.old: The kingdom does not come with outward observation — it is in your midst / among you
entries.new: Jesus says that the kingdom of God comes not with observation, neither shall they say, Lo here, or, lo there, for behold, the kingdom of God is within you.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Growth and Presence of the Kingdom
entries.old: The sower — the same seed falls on different soils and produces different responses to the kingdom message
entries.new: Jesus tells of a sower whose seed falls by the wayside and is devoured by fowls, on stony ground where it springs up but withers without root, among thorns that choke it, and on good ground where it brings forth fruit a hundredfold, sixtyfold, and thirtyfold; he then explains that the seed is the word of the kingdom and the soils are the hearers — the wayside from whom the wicked one snatches it, the stony who receive it with joy but fall away under tribulation, the thorny who are choked by the cares of this world and the deceitfulness of riches, and the good ground who hear, understand, and bear fruit.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Growth and Presence of the Kingdom
entries.old: Explains why he speaks in parables — kingdom mysteries are given to disciples but veiled to outsiders
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples that it is given unto them to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven but to others it is not given, that whoever has shall have more abundance and whoever has not shall lose even what he has, and that he therefore speaks to the multitude in parables because seeing they see not and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Growth and Presence of the Kingdom
entries.old: Wheat and tares — kingdom and evil coexist until the final harvest, when angels will separate them
entries.new: Jesus likens the kingdom of heaven to a man who sows good seed in his field while his enemy sows tares among the wheat, and tells the servants to let both grow together until the harvest, when the reapers will gather and burn the tares and gather the wheat into the barn; he then explains that the sower is the Son of man, the field the world, the good seed the children of the kingdom, the tares the children of the wicked one, the enemy the devil, the harvest the end of the world, and the reapers the angels, who at that time shall gather all things that offend out of his kingdom and cast them into a furnace of fire where there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth, while the righteous shall shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Growth and Presence of the Kingdom
entries.old: Tells the disciples that understanding the parable of the sower is the key to understanding all his parables
entries.new: Jesus asks the disciples whether they know this parable, saying that if they do not, how then will they know all parables.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Growth and Presence of the Kingdom
entries.old: Seed growing secretly — a man scatters seed; it grows without his effort until harvest
entries.new: Jesus likens the kingdom of God to a man who casts seed into the ground, then sleeps and rises night and day while the seed springs and grows up he knows not how, for the earth brings forth fruit of herself — first the blade, then the ear, then the full corn — and when the fruit is ripe he puts in the sickle, because the harvest is come.

entries.old: Unless righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, entry is impossible
entries.new: Jesus says that except his hearers' righteousness exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, they shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven.

entries.old: Seek first the kingdom and his righteousness — all else will be added; many are called but few are chosen
entries.new: Jesus charges his hearers to seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, with the promise that all these things shall be added unto them.

entries.old: Enter by the narrow gate — broad and easy is the way to destruction; few find the narrow way
entries.new: Jesus charges his hearers to enter in at the strait gate, for wide is the gate and broad the way that leads to destruction and many go in there, but strait is the gate and narrow the way that leads unto life, and few there be that find it.

entries.old: Not everyone who says “Lord, Lord” will enter — only he who does the will of the Father
entries.new: Jesus declares that not everyone who says unto him, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of his Father in heaven, and that to many who in that day plead their prophesying, casting out of devils, and wonderful works in his name, he will profess, I never knew you, depart from me, ye that work iniquity.

entries.old: Quotes Isaiah's prophecy fulfilled in dull-hearted hearers — they hear but understand not, see but perceive not, lest they be converted
entries.new: Jesus says that in his hearers is fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah, that by hearing they shall hear and not understand and seeing they shall see and not perceive, for this people's heart is waxed gross, their ears dull, and their eyes closed, lest they should see, hear, understand, be converted, and he should heal them.

entries.old: Unless one becomes like a child, he cannot enter the kingdom
entries.new: Jesus declares that except his hearers be converted and become as little children, they shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.

entries.old: It is hard for a rich person to enter the kingdom — easier for a camel through a needle's eye
entries.new: Jesus says that a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven, and that it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.

entries.old: The tax collectors and prostitutes enter the kingdom before the religious leaders who refused to believe
entries.new: Jesus declares to the chief priests and elders that the publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before them, for John came in the way of righteousness and they believed him not, but the publicans and harlots believed him, and even seeing it they did not afterward repent and believe.

entries.old: Entry requires being born again — of water and Spirit; what is born of flesh is flesh; the Spirit moves like the wind
entries.new: Jesus tells Nicodemus that except a man be born again he cannot see the kingdom of God, and except he be born of water and of the Spirit he cannot enter into the kingdom of God, for that which is born of the flesh is flesh and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit, and likens everyone born of the Spirit to the wind, which blows where it lists and whose sound is heard though none can tell whence it comes or whither it goes.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Citizens of the Kingdom — The Beatitudes
entries.old: Blessed are the poor in spirit — theirs is the kingdom of heaven
entries.new: Jesus blesses the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Citizens of the Kingdom — The Beatitudes
entries.old: Blessed are those who mourn — they shall be comforted
entries.new: Jesus blesses those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Citizens of the Kingdom — The Beatitudes
entries.old: Blessed are the meek — they shall inherit the earth
entries.new: Jesus blesses the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Citizens of the Kingdom — The Beatitudes
entries.old: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness — they shall be satisfied
entries.new: Jesus blesses those who hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Citizens of the Kingdom — The Beatitudes
entries.old: Blessed are the merciful — they shall receive mercy
entries.new: Jesus blesses the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Citizens of the Kingdom — The Beatitudes
entries.old: Blessed are the pure in heart — they shall see God
entries.new: Jesus blesses the pure in heart, for they shall see God.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Citizens of the Kingdom — The Beatitudes
entries.old: Blessed are the peacemakers — they shall be called sons of God
entries.new: Jesus blesses the peacemakers, for they shall be called the children of God.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Citizens of the Kingdom — The Beatitudes
entries.old: Blessed are those persecuted for righteousness — theirs is the kingdom; rejoice, great is the reward in heaven
entries.new: Jesus blesses those who are persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven, and tells his hearers to rejoice and be exceeding glad when men revile them, persecute them, and falsely speak all manner of evil against them for his sake, for great is their reward in heaven, since so persecuted they the prophets before them.

entries.old: The parable of the vineyard workers — all receive the same wage regardless of hours; the last shall be first
entries.new: Jesus likens the kingdom of heaven to a householder who hires labourers for his vineyard at a penny a day, going out at the third, sixth, ninth, and eleventh hours to hire still more, and at evening orders his steward to pay every man a penny beginning with the last; when those hired first murmur, he answers that he does them no wrong, for he gives to the last what he agreed with them, declaring that the last shall be first and the first last, for many are called but few chosen.

entries.old: The parable of the wicked tenants — the vineyard taken from those who killed the owner's son
entries.new: Jesus tells of a householder who plants a vineyard, lets it out to husbandmen, and goes into a far country; when he sends servants to receive the fruits, the husbandmen beat, kill, and stone them, and at last kill his son to seize the inheritance, so the lord of the vineyard will destroy those husbandmen and let it out to others; he then declares that the stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner, that the kingdom of God shall be taken from them and given to a nation bringing forth its fruits, and that whoever falls on this stone shall be broken, but on whomsoever it falls, it will grind him to powder.

entries.old: He has come to call sinners to repentance, not the righteous; unless you repent you will all likewise perish
entries.new: Jesus says that they that be whole need not a physician but they that are sick, and that he is not come to call the righteous but sinners to repentance, charging his hearers to learn what is meant by the words I will have mercy and not sacrifice.

entries.old: Pronounces woe on Chorazin and Bethsaida — Tyre and Sidon would have repented in sackcloth and ashes had they seen such mighty works
entries.new: Jesus pronounces woe upon Chorazin and Bethsaida, declaring that if the mighty works done in them had been done in Tyre and Sidon, those cities would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.

entries.old: Warns that an unclean spirit returning with seven worse spirits leaves the person's final state worse than the first
entries.new: Jesus warns that when an unclean spirit goes out of a man and walks through dry places seeking rest, it returns to find the house empty, swept, and garnished, then takes seven other spirits more wicked than itself to dwell there, so that the last state of that man is worse than the first — and so shall it be unto that wicked generation.

entries.old: Asks whether the Galileans Pilate killed were greater sinners — calls all to repent or likewise perish
entries.new: Jesus asks whether the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices were sinners above all the Galileans because they suffered such things.

entries.old: Asks whether the eighteen killed when the tower in Siloam fell were greater sinners than other Jerusalemites
entries.new: Jesus asks whether the eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem.

entries.old: Parable of the barren fig tree — the owner gives one final year to bear fruit before judgment falls
entries.new: Jesus tells of a man who had a fig tree planted in his vineyard and came three years seeking fruit on it and found none, and bid the dresser of the vineyard cut it down, but the dresser asked that it be let alone one more year while he digs about it and dungs it, and if it then bear fruit, well, and if not, after that it shall be cut down.

entries.old: There is more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than ninety-nine who need no repentance
entries.new: Jesus says that there shall be joy in heaven and in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons who need no repentance.

entries.old: Calls Zacchaeus down from the sycamore tree — he must stay at his house today
entries.new: Jesus calls Zacchaeus to make haste and come down from the sycamore tree, for he must abide at his house that day.

entries.old: Declares salvation has come to Zacchaeus's house — he too is a son of Abraham
entries.new: Jesus declares that this day is salvation come to the house of Zacchaeus, forasmuch as he also is a son of Abraham.

entries.old: He finds the healed man in the temple and warns him to sin no more lest a worse thing come upon him
entries.new: Jesus finds the healed man in the temple and says, Behold, thou art made whole; sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.

entries.old: He asks the woman where her accusers are and tells her that neither does he condemn her — go and sin no more
entries.new: Jesus asks the woman where her accusers are and whether any man has condemned her, then tells her that neither does he condemn her — go, and sin no more.

entries.old: Lost sheep — a shepherd leaves ninety-nine to search for the one; rejoices when found
entries.new: Jesus tells of a man with a hundred sheep who, losing one, leaves the ninety and nine in the wilderness and goes after the lost one until he finds it, then lays it on his shoulders rejoicing and calls his friends and neighbours to rejoice with him, saying that likewise there shall be more joy in heaven over one sinner that repenteth than over ninety and nine just persons who need no repentance.

entries.old: Lost coin — a woman searches the whole house; calls her neighbors when found
entries.new: Jesus tells of a woman who, having ten pieces of silver and losing one, lights a candle, sweeps the house, and seeks diligently until she finds it, then calls her friends and neighbours to rejoice with her, and says that likewise there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.

entries.old: Lost son — a son returns from ruin; his father runs to meet him and restores him fully
entries.new: Jesus tells of a man with two sons, the younger of whom takes his portion of goods into a far country and wastes his substance with riotous living until, in famine and feeding swine, he comes to himself and resolves to return to his father confessing he has sinned against heaven and is no more worthy to be called a son; the father, seeing him while yet a great way off, has compassion and runs and falls on his neck and kisses him, and calls for the best robe, a ring, shoes, and the fatted calf, declaring that this his son was dead and is alive again, was lost and is found; the elder son, returning from the field and hearing the music and dancing, is angry and refuses to go in, complaining that he has served many years without such a feast, but the father entreats him, saying, Son, thou art ever with me and all that I have is thine, and that it was meet to make merry, for thy brother was dead and is alive again, and was lost and is found.

entries.old: Come to me, all who are weary and burdened — take my yoke and learn from me; I am gentle and lowly; my yoke is easy and burden light
entries.new: Jesus calls all that labour and are heavy laden to come unto him and he will give them rest, bidding them take his yoke upon them and learn of him, for he is meek and lowly in heart, and they shall find rest unto their souls, for his yoke is easy and his burden is light.

entries.old: Promises that all whom the Father gives him will come to him, and whoever comes he will never cast out
entries.new: Jesus promises that all that the Father giveth him shall come to him, and that him that cometh to him he will in no wise cast out.

entries.old: The Spirit moves like the wind — its origin and destination unseen; so it is with everyone born of the Spirit
entries.new: Jesus tells Nicodemus to marvel not that he must be born again, for the wind blows where it wills and one hears its sound but cannot tell from where it comes or where it goes, and so is every one that is born of the Spirit.

entries.old: Rebukes Nicodemus, a teacher of Israel, for not understanding — if earthly things baffle, how can heavenly things be received?
entries.new: Jesus rebukes Nicodemus as a master of Israel who knows not these things, declaring that he and his speak what they know and testify of what they have seen but their witness is not received, and asks how they shall believe heavenly things if they believe not when he tells them earthly things.

entries.old: Identifies the unbelief in their midst — no one can come to him unless granted by the Father
entries.new: Jesus says that there are some among his hearers who do not believe, and therefore he has told them that no man can come to him except it were given to him of the Father.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Faith as the Condition of Salvation
entries.old: Whoever believes in the Son shall not perish but have eternal life and will not be judged; whoever rejects him will not see life
entries.new: Jesus declares that God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believes in him should not perish but have everlasting life, that God sent not his Son to condemn the world but that the world through him might be saved, and that he who believes on him is not condemned but he who believes not is condemned already because he has not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Faith as the Condition of Salvation
entries.old: I am the resurrection and the life — whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live; whoever lives and believes shall never die
entries.new: Jesus declares to Martha that he is the resurrection and the life, that he who believes in him though he were dead yet shall he live, and that whosoever lives and believes in him shall never die.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Faith as the Condition of Salvation
entries.old: Urges the crowd to walk and believe while the light is with them, so they may become children of light
entries.new: Jesus urges his hearers that yet a little while is the light with them, charging them to walk while they have the light lest darkness come upon them, for he who walks in darkness knows not where he goes, and to believe in the light while they have it that they may be the children of light.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Eternal Life — Its Nature and Assurance
entries.old: Promises that the water he gives will become a spring of water welling up to eternal life — those who drink it will never thirst again
entries.new: Jesus tells the Samaritan woman that whosoever drinks of the water he shall give him shall never thirst, and that the water he gives shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Eternal Life — Its Nature and Assurance
entries.old: Rebukes the crowd for chasing him after the loaves — work not for perishable food but for food that lasts to eternal life
entries.new: Jesus rebukes the crowd that they seek him not because they saw the miracles but because they ate of the loaves and were filled, charging them to labor not for the meat which perishes but for the meat that endures to everlasting life, which the Son of man shall give them, for him has God the Father sealed.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Eternal Life — Its Nature and Assurance
entries.old: All taught by the Father come to him — only the one from God has seen the Father, and whoever believes has eternal life
entries.new: Jesus says it is written in the prophets that they shall be all taught of God, and every man therefore who has heard and learned of the Father comes to him, that no man has seen the Father save he who is of God, and that he who believes on him has everlasting life.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Eternal Life — Its Nature and Assurance
entries.old: Whoever commits sin is the servant of sin, and the servant does not abide in the house forever, but the Son abides forever
entries.new: Jesus declares that whosoever commits sin is the servant of sin, and that the servant abides not in the house for ever but the Son abides ever.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Eternal Life — Its Nature and Assurance
entries.old: He has no devil but honors his Father; he seeks not his own glory, and if any man keeps his saying, he shall never see death
entries.new: Jesus says that he has no devil but honors his Father while they dishonor him, that he seeks not his own glory but there is one who seeks and judges, and that if a man keep his saying he shall never see death.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Eternal Life — Its Nature and Assurance
entries.old: Contrasts the thief who comes to destroy with himself — he came so they may have life abundantly
entries.new: Jesus says the thief comes only to steal and to kill and to destroy, but he is come that they might have life and have it more abundantly.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Eternal Life — Its Nature and Assurance
entries.old: My sheep hear my voice — I know them, they follow me, I give them eternal life; no one can snatch them from my hand
entries.new: Jesus declares that his sheep hear his voice and he knows them and they follow him, and that he gives them eternal life and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of his hand.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Eternal Life — Its Nature and Assurance
entries.old: In my Father's house are many rooms — he goes to prepare a place and will come again to receive his own
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples that in his Father's house are many mansions, that he goes to prepare a place for them, and that if he goes and prepares a place he will come again and receive them to himself, that where he is they may be also.

entries.old: Enter by the narrow gate — broad and easy is the way to destruction; the narrow way leads to life and few find it
entries.new: Jesus charges his hearers to enter in at the strait gate, for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction and many go in by it, but strait is the gate and narrow is the way that leads to life and few there be that find it.

entries.old: Not everyone who says “Lord, Lord” will enter — only he who does the will of the Father; many are called, few chosen
entries.new: Jesus declares that not every one who says to him Lord, Lord shall enter into the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of his Father in heaven, and that many will say to him in that day Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in your name and cast out devils and done many wonderful works, and he will profess to them, I never knew you, depart from me ye that work iniquity.

entries.old: Warns that once the master shuts the door, those who only knew him casually will be told 'I never knew you'
entries.new: Jesus warns that when once the master of the house has risen up and shut the door, those who stand without and knock saying Lord, Lord, open to us, will hear him answer that he knows them not from where they are, and though they protest that they ate and drank in his presence and he taught in their streets, he will say, I tell you, I know you not from where you are; depart from me, all you workers of iniquity.

entries.old: Calls Herod a fox and laments over Jerusalem — how often he longed to gather her children, but they refused
entries.new: Jesus charges his hearers to tell that fox Herod that he casts out devils and does cures today and tomorrow and the third day shall be perfected, that he must walk today and tomorrow and the day following for a prophet cannot perish out of Jerusalem, and laments over Jerusalem who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, saying how often he would have gathered her children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, but they would not, and that her house is left to her desolate, and she shall not see him until the time when she says, Blessed is he that comes in the name of the Lord.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: Heals the centurion's servant from a distance — let it be done as he has believed
entries.new: Jesus tells the centurion to go his way, and that as he has believed, so be it done unto him.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: Tests the two blind men's faith before healing them
entries.new: Jesus asks the two blind men whether they believe that he is able to do this.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.new: Jesus declares to those he heals that according to their faith be it unto them, and tells the woman with the issue of blood and others that their faith has made them whole and saved them, sending them away in peace.
entries.old: According to your faith let it be done — your faith has saved / healed you

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: Bids Peter walk on the water — Come
entries.new: Jesus calls Peter out of the boat onto the water with a single word: come.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: Tests the Canaanite woman — it is not meet to take the children's bread, and to cast it to dogs
entries.new: Jesus says to the Canaanite woman that it is not meet to take the children's bread and to cast it to dogs.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: Praises the Canaanite woman's great faith and grants her request
entries.new: Jesus praises the Canaanite woman, declaring great is her faith and that it shall be unto her even as she will.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: Faith like a mustard seed can move mountains — nothing will be impossible; whatever is asked with belief will be received
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples that if they have faith as a grain of mustard seed they shall say to a mountain remove hence and it shall remove, and nothing shall be impossible unto them, and that whatsoever they ask in prayer believing, they shall receive.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: Rewards the Syrophoenician woman's faith — the demon has gone out of her daughter
entries.new: Jesus tells the Syrophoenician woman that for her saying she may go her way, for the devil is gone out of her daughter.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: Rebukes a faithless generation, questions the scribes and the boy\u2019s father, and declares that all things are possible to the one who believes
entries.new: Jesus laments a faithless generation and asks how long he shall suffer them, calls the boy to be brought to him, asks the father how long he has been thus, and declares that if he can believe, all things are possible to him that believes.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: I have not found so great faith — no, not in Israel — Jesus marvels at the centurion
entries.new: Jesus marvels at the centurion and declares that he has not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: Tells the bleeding woman her faith has made her whole — go in peace
entries.new: Jesus tells the woman to be of good comfort, that her faith has made her whole, and bids her go in peace.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: Calls a faithless and perverse generation to bring the demon-tormented son to him
entries.new: Jesus cries out against a faithless and perverse generation, asking how long he shall be with them and suffer them, and bids the father bring his son to him.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: When the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on earth? Blessed are those who have not seen and yet believed
entries.new: Jesus asks whether, when the Son of man comes, he shall find faith on the earth, and pronounces blessed those who have not seen and yet have believed.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: He declares that the work of God is to believe on the one whom God has sent
entries.new: Jesus declares that this is the work of God, that they believe on him whom he has sent.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: He tells the crowd that even though they have seen him, they do not believe
entries.new: Jesus tells the crowd that they have seen him and yet do not believe.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: He finds the cast-out man and asks him whether he believes on the Son of God
entries.new: Jesus seeks out the man cast out by the Pharisees and asks him whether he believes on the Son of God.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: Tells the unbelieving Jews they do not believe because they are not among his sheep
entries.new: Jesus tells the Jews that they do not believe because they are not of his sheep, as he had said unto them.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: Tells the disciples plainly that Lazarus is dead — and is glad for their sakes, that they may believe
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples plainly that Lazarus is dead, and says he is glad for their sakes that he was not there, to the intent that they may believe, and bids them go unto him.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Nature and Power of Faith
entries.old: He who believes in Jesus shall do the works he does, and greater works, because he goes to the Father.
entries.new: Jesus declares that he who believes on him shall do the works that he does, and greater works than these, because he goes unto the Father.

entries.old: Reassures the disciples on the storm-tossed sea — be of good cheer, it is I, be not afraid
entries.new: Jesus calls out to the disciples on the storm-tossed sea, telling them to be of good cheer, that it is he, and to be not afraid.

entries.old: Rebukes the disciples' little faith — do they not remember the loaves of the five thousand and the four thousand?
entries.new: Jesus rebukes the disciples as of little faith for reasoning that they have brought no bread, and asks whether they do not remember the five loaves of the five thousand and the seven loaves of the four thousand and how many baskets they took up.

entries.old: Laments the unbelieving generation and calls the boy to be brought to him for healing
entries.new: Jesus cries out against a faithless and perverse generation, asking how long he shall be with them and suffer them, and bids the boy be brought to him.

entries.old: Directs the disciples to cross the Sea of Galilee — setting up the storm-stilling miracle
entries.new: Jesus tells the disciples, let us pass over unto the other side of the sea.

entries.old: Why are you afraid? Why did you doubt? O you of little faith — do not be afraid, only believe
entries.new: Jesus asks his disciples why they are so fearful and how it is that they have no faith, charges Peter as of little faith asking why he doubted, and tells the ruler of the synagogue not to be afraid but only believe.

entries.old: Be of good cheer: it is I; be not afraid — Jesus reassures the disciples as he walks on the sea
entries.new: Jesus calls out to the disciples as he walks upon the sea, telling them to be of good cheer, that it is he, and to be not afraid.

entries.old: Do not be afraid, little flock — it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom; stop doubting and believe
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples to fear not, little flock, for it is the Father's good pleasure to give them the kingdom, and charges Thomas to be not faithless but believing.

entries.old: He rebukes the nobleman, saying that unless they see signs and wonders, they will not believe
entries.new: Jesus says to the nobleman that except they see signs and wonders, they will not believe.

entries.old: He calls out to the terrified disciples on the sea, saying it is I — be not afraid
entries.new: Jesus calls out to the terrified disciples on the sea, telling them it is he and to be not afraid.

entries.old: Do not be anxious about life — food, drink, or clothing; life is more than these things; the Father knows what you need
entries.new: Jesus charges his hearers to take no thought for their life, what they shall eat or drink, nor for their body, what they shall put on, declaring that the life is more than meat and the body than raiment, and that the heavenly Father knows they have need of all these things.

entries.old: Consider the birds the Father feeds and the lilies clothed better than Solomon — how much more will he clothe you
entries.new: Jesus bids his hearers behold the fowls of the air whom the heavenly Father feeds though they neither sow nor reap, and consider the lilies of the field arrayed beyond Solomon in all his glory, asking if God so clothes the grass shall he not much more clothe them, O ye of little faith.

entries.old: Seek first the kingdom and his righteousness — all else will be added; do not worry about tomorrow
entries.new: Jesus charges his hearers to seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto them, and to take no thought for the morrow, for sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.

entries.old: Do not be anxious about what to say when brought before rulers — the Spirit of the Father will speak through you in that hour
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples that when they are delivered up they should take no thought how or what they shall speak, for it shall be given them in that hour, and it is not they that speak but the Spirit of their Father which speaks in them.

entries.old: Do not let your hearts be troubled — peace I leave with you; in this world you will have tribulation, but I have overcome the world
entries.new: Jesus tells his disciples to let not their heart be troubled but to believe in God and in him, leaves them his peace not as the world gives, and declares that in the world they shall have tribulation but to be of good cheer for he has overcome the world.

entries.old: Turns the lawyer's question back on him — what does the law itself say?
entries.new: Jesus answers the lawyer's question with a question, asking what is written in the law and how he reads it.

entries.old: Marks John the Baptist as the hinge — Law and Prophets ended with him, the kingdom is now preached
entries.new: Jesus declares that the law and the prophets were until John, and that since then the kingdom of God is preached and every man presses into it.

entries.old: Affirms the enduring authority of the Law — sooner heaven and earth pass than its smallest stroke fail
entries.new: Jesus declares that it is easier for heaven and earth to pass than for one tittle of the law to fail.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Moses and the Scriptures Pointing to Jesus
entries.old: If they believed Moses, they would believe him — Moses wrote about him; as Moses lifted up the serpent, so must the Son of Man be lifted up
entries.new: Jesus says that if his hearers had believed Moses they would have believed him, for Moses wrote of him, and asks how they will believe his words if they do not believe his writings.

entries.subcategoryTitle: Moses and the Scriptures Pointing to Jesus
entries.old: Abraham rejoiced to see his day; the Scriptures bear witness about him — yet they refuse to come to him
entries.new: Jesus declares that their father Abraham rejoiced to see his day, and that he saw it and was glad.

entries.old: This cup is my blood of the covenant — the new covenant in my blood, poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins; do this in remembrance of me
entries.new: Jesus declares that the cup is his blood of the new testament, shed for many for the remission of sins.

entries.old: Pledges he will not drink the cup again until he drinks it new in the Father's kingdom
entries.new: Jesus pledges that he will not drink henceforth of the fruit of the vine until that day when he drinks it new with his disciples in his Father's kingdom.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching
entries.old: He tells the woman that if she knew the gift of God and who was speaking with her, she would have asked him for living water
entries.new: Jesus tells the Samaritan woman that if she knew the gift of God and who it is that asks her for a drink, she would have asked him and he would have given her living water.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching
entries.old: He says whoever drinks of this well water will thirst again, contrasting it with the living water he gives
entries.new: Jesus says that whoever drinks of the well water shall thirst again.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching
entries.old: Corrects the crowd — it was the Father, not Moses, who gives the true bread from heaven that gives life to the world
entries.new: Jesus corrects the crowd that Moses did not give them the bread from heaven, but his Father gives the true bread from heaven, for the bread of God is he which comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching
entries.old: Declares himself the living bread from heaven — his flesh is given for the life of the world
entries.new: Jesus declares that he is the bread of life and the living bread which came down from heaven, and that the bread he will give is his flesh, given for the life of the world, so that whoever comes to him shall never hunger and whoever believes on him shall never thirst.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching
entries.old: Their fathers ate manna in the wilderness and died, but this is the bread that comes down from heaven so that one may eat of it and not die
entries.new: Jesus says that their fathers ate manna in the wilderness and are dead, but the bread which comes down from heaven is such that a man may eat of it and not die.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching
entries.old: Unless one eats the flesh of the Son of Man and drinks his blood, he has no life in him
entries.new: Jesus declares that unless they eat the flesh of the Son of man and drink his blood, they have no life in them.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching
entries.old: Whoever eats his flesh and drinks his blood has eternal life — his flesh is true food, his blood is true drink; they abide in him and he in them
entries.new: Jesus says that whoever eats his flesh and drinks his blood has eternal life and will be raised up at the last day, for his flesh is meat indeed and his blood is drink indeed, and such a one dwells in him and he in them.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching
entries.old: Promises that whoever feeds on him will live by him forever — unlike the manna eaten by ancestors who died
entries.new: Jesus promises that as the living Father has sent him and he lives by the Father, so whoever eats him shall live by him, and unlike the fathers who ate manna and are dead, he who eats this bread shall live for ever.

entries.subcategoryTitle: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching
entries.old: Clarifies that his Bread of Life teaching is spiritual — the Spirit gives life, the flesh profits nothing
entries.new: Jesus clarifies that it is the Spirit that gives life and the flesh profits nothing, and that the words he speaks to them are spirit and life.

entries.subcategoryTitle: New and Old — The Covenant Transition
entries.old: Teaches that new wine must go into new wineskins — the new covenant cannot be poured into old structures
entries.new: Jesus asks whether the children of the bridechamber can mourn while the bridegroom is with them, then teaches that no man puts a piece of new cloth on an old garment lest the rent be made worse, and that men do not put new wine into old bottles lest the bottles break and the wine be spilled, but pour new wine into new bottles so both are preserved.
